title.zh: 卷二十六 列傳第十六 袁湛
title.raw: 卷二十六 列傳第十六 袁湛 Volume 26 Biographies 16: Yuan Zhan

sentences.zh: 宋武帝起兵，以為鎮軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised his army, Yuan Zhan was appointed Staff Adviser to the Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched to seize power, Yuan Zhan was made a staff adviser on the pacifying army.

sentences.zh: 以從征功，封晉寧縣五等男。

translations.literal: For merit in following the campaigns, he was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Baron of Jinning County.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign service earned him the title Fifth-Rank Baron of Jinning.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi, he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 12 he was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 武帝北伐，湛兼太尉，與兼司空尚書范泰奉九命禮物拜授武帝，帝沖讓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu marched north, Zhan served concurrently as Grand Commandant; together with Fan Tai, who held concurrent posts as Minister of Works and Master of Writing, he presented the nine tokens of investiture to the emperor, who modestly declined.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern expedition Zhan doubled as Grand Commandant. He and Fan Tai—concurrently Minister of Works and Master of Writing—brought the nine regalia of kingship to Liu Yu, who refused them with feigned humility.

sentences.zh: 湛等隨軍至洛陽，住柏谷塢。

translations.literal: Zhan and the others followed the army to Luoyang and lodged at the Baigu stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan went on with the army to Luoyang and quartered at Baigu Fort.

sentences.zh: 泰議受使未畢，不拜晉帝諸陵，湛獨至五陵展敬，時人美之。

translations.literal: Tai argued that their mission was not yet complete and that they should not pay homage at the Jin emperors' tombs; Zhan alone went to the Five Tombs to show reverence, and men praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai held that their embassy was unfinished and they ought not visit the Jin imperial tombs; Zhan alone went to the Five Tombs to pay respects, and contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 子淳，淳子植，並早卒。

translations.literal: His son Chun, and Chun's son Zhi, both died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun and Chun's son Zhi both died in youth.

sentences.zh: 弟 豹

translations.literal: Younger brother Bao
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Bao

sentences.zh: 湛弟豹字士蔚，好學博聞，善談雅俗。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Bao, styled Shiyu, loved learning and was widely informed, skilled in discussing refined and common matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Bao, courtesy name Shiyu, was a learned and well-read man, adept at talk of high culture and everyday life alike.

sentences.zh: 每商較古今，兼以誦詠，聽者忘疲。

translations.literal: Whenever he compared past and present and added recitation, listeners forgot their fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: In debate over past and present, laced with poetry recited aloud, his listeners forgot weariness.

sentences.zh: 為御史中丞時，鄱陽縣侯孟懷玉上母檀拜國太夫人，有司奏許。

translations.literal: When he was Censor-in-Chief, Marquis Meng Huaiyu of Poyang petitioned to have his mother Tan ennobled as Grand Lady of the State; the relevant offices memorialized approval.
translations.idiomatic: As Censor-in-Chief, he heard that Marquis Meng Huaiyu of Poyang had asked that his mother Tan be made Grand Lady of the State; the ministries recommended granting it.

sentences.zh: 豹以婦人從夫爵，懷玉父大司農綽見居列卿，妻不宜從子。

translations.literal: Bao held that a woman follows her husband's rank; Huaiyu's father Chuo, Grand Minister of Agriculture, already stood among senior ministers, so the wife ought not take rank from the son.
translations.idiomatic: Bao argued that a wife takes rank from her husband; since Huaiyu's father Chuo already served among the chief ministers, the mother should not derive her title from the son.

sentences.zh: 奏免尚書右僕射劉柳等官，詔並贖論。

translations.literal: He memorialized to dismiss Vice Director Liu Liu and others from office; an edict ordered them all ransomed instead.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted impeachment of Vice Director Liu Liu and others; the throne commuted all to fines.

sentences.zh: 後為丹陽尹，太尉長史，義熙九年，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he served as Prefect of Danyang and Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant; in the ninth year of Yixi he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Prefect of Danyang and chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, and died in office in Yixi 9.

sentences.zh: 以參伐蜀謀，追封南昌縣五等子。

translations.literal: For his part in planning the conquest of Shu, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Viscount of Nanchang County.
translations.idiomatic: For helping plan the Shu campaign he was posthumously made Fifth-Rank Viscount of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 子淑。

translations.literal: Son Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shu.

sentences.zh: 豹子 淑

translations.literal: Bao's son Shu
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son Shu

sentences.zh: 淑字陽源，少有風氣。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Yangyuan, from youth had spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, showed force of character even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，伯父湛謂人曰：「此非凡兒。

translations.literal: When he was only a few years old, his uncle Zhan said to others, "This is no ordinary child."
translations.idiomatic: At only a few years old his uncle Zhan told people, "This is no ordinary child."

sentences.zh: 」至十餘歲，為姑夫王弘所賞，博涉多通，不為章句學。

translations.literal: By his teens he won the admiration of his uncle by marriage Wang Hong; he read broadly and mastered much, without pursuing the exegetical school.
translations.idiomatic: In his teens his uncle by marriage Wang Hong took notice of him. He read widely and understood much, but never bothered with commentarial pedantry.

sentences.zh: 文采遒豔，從橫有才辯。

translations.literal: His literary style was vigorous and brilliant; in debate he was resourceful and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: His prose ran bold and bright; in argument he was quick and sharp.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康命為司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang appointed him Libationer of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng made him Libationer of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 義康不好文學，雖外相禮接，意好甚疏。

translations.literal: Yikang did not care for letters; though outwardly courteous, inwardly he was quite distant.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang cared little for literature; he kept polite appearances but felt little warmth toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 從母兄劉湛欲其附己，而淑不為改意，由是大相乖失。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, elder son of Shu's mother's sister, wished Shu to attach himself to him, but Shu would not change his stance, and from this they fell greatly apart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, a cousin on Shu's mother's side, wanted Shu in his camp; Shu refused to shift allegiance, and the two became bitterly estranged.

sentences.zh: 淑乃賦詩曰：「種蘭忌當門，懷璧莫向楚。

translations.literal: Shu then composed a poem saying, "Plant orchids, but not before the gate; carry a jade, but not toward Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote a poem: "Orchids wither at the doorway; jade carried into Chu brings ruin."

sentences.zh: 楚少別玉人，門非植蘭所。

translations.literal: Chu has few who can tell jade from stone; the gate is no place to plant orchids.
translations.idiomatic: Chu knows little of jade; a gate is no bed for orchids.

sentences.zh: 」尋以久疾免官。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of long illness, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long chronic illness cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，累遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 26 he rose by stages to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其秋大舉北侵，從容曰：「今當席捲趙、魏，檢玉岱宗，願上封禪書一篇。

translations.literal: That autumn a great northern campaign was launched; he said calmly, "Now we shall sweep Zhao and Wei and gather jade at Mount Tai; I wish to submit a memorial on the feng and shan rites."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the court launched a major northern offensive. Shu remarked calmly, "We are about to roll up Zhao and Wei and gather tribute at Mount Tai—I should like to draft a fengshan memorial."

sentences.zh: 」文帝曰：「盛德之事，我何足以當之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said, "Such a deed of supreme virtue—how could I be worthy of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen replied, "A deed of supreme virtue? I am hardly equal to that."

sentences.zh: 」出為始興王浚征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Chief Clerk on Prince Jun of Shixing's northern campaign staff and Administrator of Eastern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as chief clerk on Prince Jun of Shixing's northern staff and as Administrator of Eastern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 淑始到府，浚引見謂曰：「不意舅遂垂屈佐？

translations.literal: When Shu first arrived at the princely residence, Jun received him and said, "I never thought my uncle would stoop to serve as my aide?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shu first reported to the princely household, Jun received him and said, "I never expected my uncle would condescend to assist me."

sentences.zh: 」淑答曰：「朝廷遣下官，本以光公府望也。

translations.literal: Shu answered, "The court sent me down precisely to lend luster to your household's standing."
translations.idiomatic: Shu answered, "The court sent me here to burnish your house's prestige."

sentences.zh: 」還為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He returned and became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時魏軍南伐至瓜步，文帝使百官議防禦之術，淑上議，其言甚誕。

translations.literal: When Wei armies marched south as far as Guabu, Emperor Wen had the officials debate measures of defense; Shu submitted a plan whose language was very extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei forces pushed south to Guabu, Emperor Wen ordered the bureaucracy to debate defense; Shu's memorial was wildly grandiloquent.

sentences.zh: 淑喜誇，每為時人所嘲。

translations.literal: Shu loved to boast, and people often mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu loved grand talk, and contemporaries often ridiculed him for it.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗送錢三萬餉淑，一宿復遣人追取，謂為使人謬誤，欲以戲淑，淑與浚書曰：「聞之前志曰，『七年之中，一與一奪，義士猶或非之』。

translations.literal: Prince Jun of Shixing once sent thirty thousand cash as a gift to Shu; after one night he sent men to take it back, saying a messenger had erred and wishing to tease Shu; Shu wrote to Jun, "I have read in earlier records that 'within seven years, one grant and one withdrawal—even a man of honor may fault it.'"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun once sent Shu thirty thousand cash; overnight he sent men to reclaim it, claiming a clerk's mistake and intending a jest. Shu wrote back: "Old records say that within seven years, one gift and one recall—even an honorable man may take offense."

sentences.zh: 況密邇旬次，何其裒益之亟也。

translations.literal: How much the more when, within scarcely ten days, gain and loss come so swiftly!
translations.idiomatic: All the more when, in barely ten days, gifts are given and snatched away with such haste!

sentences.zh: 竊恐二三諸候有以觀大國之政。

translations.literal: I fear the feudal lords may draw from this some view of the great state's governance.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the regional lords will read in this something about how the great state is governed.

sentences.zh: 」遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 元凶將為逆，其夜淑在直，呼淑及蕭斌等，流涕告以「明旦當行大事，望相與戮力」。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was about to rebel, that night Shu was on palace duty; the prince summoned Shu and Xiao Bin and others, weeping as he told them, "Tomorrow at dawn I shall act; I hope you will strive together with me."
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his coup the Crown Prince Liu Shao summoned Shu and Xiao Bin while Shu was on palace duty, weeping as he said, "At dawn I act—stand with me."

sentences.zh: 淑、斌並曰：「自古無此，願加善思。

translations.literal: Shu and Bin both said, "From antiquity there has never been such a thing; please think again carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Bin both said, "Nothing like this exists in history—think again."

sentences.zh: 」劭怒，斌懼曰：「謹奉令。

translations.literal: Shao grew angry; Bin, afraid, said, "We obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: Shao flew into rage; Bin, terrified, said, "Your order is obeyed."

sentences.zh: 」淑叱之曰：「卿便謂殿下真有是邪？

translations.literal: Shu rebuked him, saying, "Do you really believe His Highness means this?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu snapped at him: "You truly think the prince means it?"

sentences.zh: 殿下幼時嘗患風，或是疾動耳。

translations.literal: When the prince was young he once suffered wind illness; perhaps this is only a flare of the old sickness.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy the prince had wind sickness—perhaps this is only the old ailment returning.

sentences.zh: 」劭愈怒，因問曰：「事當克不？

translations.literal: Shao grew still angrier and asked, "Will the affair succeed or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao grew angrier still and demanded, "Will it succeed?"

sentences.zh: 」淑曰：「居不疑之地，何患不克；

translations.literal: Shu said, "Occupying a position free of suspicion, why fear failure?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "In an unquestioned position, how could it fail?"

sentences.zh: 但既克之後，為天地所不容，大禍亦旋至耳。

translations.literal: But once it succeeds, you will not be tolerated by Heaven and earth, and great disaster will swiftly follow.
translations.idiomatic: But once it succeeds, Heaven and earth will not abide you, and ruin will come at once.

sentences.zh: 」劭左右引淑衣曰：「此是何事，而可言罷。

translations.literal: Shao's attendants pulled at Shu's robe and said, "What affair is this, that you may speak and stop?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao's attendants tugged Shu's sleeve: "What business is this, that you may speak and then stop?"

sentences.zh: 」劭因起，賜淑等褲褶，又就主衣取錦，裁三尺為一段，又中裂之，分斌與淑及左右，使以縛褲褶。

translations.literal: Shao then rose and bestowed on Shu and the others trousers and jackets; he also took brocade from the wardrobe master, cut it into three-foot lengths, split each length down the middle, divided them among Bin, Shu, and the attendants, and had them use the strips to bind the trousers and jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Shao rose and gave Shu and the rest military dress; then he took brocade from the wardrobe, cut three-foot lengths, split each in two, shared them among Bin, Shu, and the attendants, and had them bind the garments with the strips.

sentences.zh: 淑出還省，繞床至四更乃寢。

translations.literal: Shu went out and returned to his office, pacing around his bed until the fourth watch before sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Shu returned to his office and paced his room until the fourth watch before lying down.

sentences.zh: 劭將出，已與蕭斌同載，呼淑甚急，淑眠終不起。

translations.literal: When Shao was about to set out, already in the carriage with Xiao Bin, he urgently summoned Shu, but Shu slept on and never rose.
translations.idiomatic: As Shao prepared to march, already in the carriage with Xiao Bin, he urgently called Shu—but Shu slept on and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 劭停車奉化門，催之相續。

translations.literal: Shao halted the carriage at Fenghua Gate and sent summons after summons.
translations.idiomatic: Shao stopped at Fenghua Gate and sent summons after summons.

sentences.zh: 徐起至車後，劭使登車，辭不上。

translations.literal: Shu slowly rose and came behind the carriage; Shao had him mount, but he declined and would not get in.
translations.idiomatic: Shu at last rose and came behind the carriage; Shao ordered him aboard, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 劭命左右殺之於奉化門外槐樹下。

translations.literal: Shao ordered his attendants to kill him beneath the pagoda tree outside Fenghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shao ordered his men to kill him under the pagoda tree outside Fenghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 劭即位，追贈太常。

translations.literal: When Shao took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Shu as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao seized the throne he posthumously made Shu Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，贈侍中、太尉，諡曰忠憲公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded, Shu was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Duke of Loyal Integrity.

sentences.zh: 又詔淑及徐湛之、江湛、王僧綽、卜天與四家長給稟。

translations.literal: An edict also granted permanent stipends to the eldest sons of the four households of Shu, Xu Zhizhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo, and Bu Tianyu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also granted permanent stipends to the eldest sons of the households of Shu, Xu Zhizhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo, and Bu Tianyu.

sentences.zh: 淑文集傳於世。

translations.literal: Shu's collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 諸子並早卒。

translations.literal: All his sons likewise died young.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons likewise died young.

sentences.zh: 兄洵子 顗

translations.literal: Elder brother Xun's son Yan
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Xun's son Yan

sentences.zh: 兄洵，吳郡太守，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Elder brother Xun, Administrator of Wu Commandery, posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The elder brother Xun, Administrator of Wu, bore the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 洵子顗。

translations.literal: Xun's son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's son Yan.

sentences.zh: 顗字國章，初為豫州主簿，累遷晉陵太守，襲南昌縣五等子。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Guozhang, first served as Chief Clerk of Yuzhou; he was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Jinling and inherited the Fifth-Rank Viscountate of Nanchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, courtesy name Guozhang, began as chief clerk of Yuzhou, rose to Administrator of Jinling, and inherited the Fifth-Rank Viscountate of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 大明末，拜侍中，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the late Daming era he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently Commander of the Vanguard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daming reign he became Palace Attendant and Commander of the Vanguard Army.

sentences.zh: 時新安王子鸞以母嬖有盛寵，太子在東宮多過，上微有廢太子立子鸞之意，從容言之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Xin'an Ziluan, because his mother was a favorite and greatly favored, and the crown prince in the Eastern Palace often transgressed, the emperor quietly harbored the idea of deposing the crown prince and installing Ziluan, and spoke of it at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziluan of Xin'an enjoyed his mother's favor; the crown prince in the Eastern Palace often misbehaved, and the emperor quietly considered replacing him with Ziluan and spoke of it in passing.

sentences.zh: 顗盛稱太子好學，有日新之美。

translations.literal: Yan greatly praised the crown prince's love of learning and daily renewal of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan spoke warmly of the crown prince's love of learning and daily improvement.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，振衣而入，顗亦厲色而出。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, shook out his robes, and went inside; Yan too went out with stern countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flared in anger, shook out his robes, and stalked within; Yan marched out with a hard face.

sentences.zh: 左丞徐爰言於帝，請宥之，帝意解。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Xu Ai spoke to the emperor and asked that Yan be pardoned; the emperor's mind eased.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Xu Ai pleaded for Yan, and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 後帝又以沈慶之才用不多，言論頗相嗤毀，顗又陳慶之忠勤有幹略，堪當重任。

translations.literal: Later the emperor again belittled Shen Qingzhi as lacking much talent, speaking with considerable mockery; Yan again declared that Qingzhi was loyal, diligent, and capable, fit for heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor again mocked Shen Qingzhi as insufficiently talented; Yan insisted Qingzhi was loyal, diligent, and capable of great trust.

sentences.zh: 由是前廢帝深感顗，慶之亦懷其德。

translations.literal: From this the deposed emperor felt deep gratitude toward Yan, and Qingzhi too cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the future Deposed Emperor felt deep gratitude toward Yan, and Qingzhi too remembered his favor.

sentences.zh: 胡以南運未至，軍士匱乏，就顗換襄陽之資。

translations.literal: Because southern transport had not yet arrived and the soldiers were exhausted of supplies, Hu sought to exchange Yan's resources at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: With southern supplies not yet arrived and the army short of provisions, Liu Hu asked to draw on Yan's stores at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 顗答曰：「都下兩宅未成，方應經理，不可損徹。

translations.literal: Yan answered, "My two residences in the capital are not yet finished and still need tending; they cannot be stripped bare."
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "My two houses in the capital are unfinished and still need upkeep—I cannot strip them bare."

sentences.zh: 」又信往來之言，言都下米貴，斗至數百，以為不勞攻伐，行自離散，於是擁甲以待之。

translations.literal: He also believed reports going back and forth that rice in the capital was dear, a peck costing several hundred, and thought there was no need to attack—the enemy would scatter of themselves; so he sat in armor and waited.
translations.idiomatic: He also believed rumors that rice in the capital had soared to hundreds per peck and that no assault was needed—the foe would break up on its own—so he sat armored and waited.

sentences.zh: 明帝使顗舊門生徐碩奉手詔譬顗曰：「卿未經為臣，今追蹤竇融，猶未晚也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Yan's former student Xu Shuo with a handwritten edict to persuade him, saying, "You have not yet truly been a subject; now to follow Dou Rong's example is still not too late."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Yan's old student Xu Shuo with a handwritten edict: "You have never truly submitted; to follow Dou Rong's example is still not too late."

sentences.zh: 」及劉胡叛走不告顗，顗至夜方知，大怒，罵曰：「今年為小子所誤。

translations.literal: When Liu Hu rebelled and fled without informing Yan, Yan learned only at night and raged, cursing, "This year I was undone by that boy."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hu rebelled and fled without telling him, Yan learned only at night and raged: "This year that boy ruined me."

sentences.zh: 」呼取飛燕，謂其眾曰：「我當自出追之。

translations.literal: He called for his horse Feiyan and told his followers, "I shall go out myself in pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: He called for his horse Feiyan and told his men, "I will ride out after them myself."

sentences.zh: 」因又遁走。

translations.literal: Then he too fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then he too fled.

sentences.zh: 至鵲頭，與戍主薛伯珍及其所領數千，步取青林，欲向尋陽。

translations.literal: Reaching Que tou, with the garrison commander Xue Bozhen and the several thousand men under his command, he went on foot toward Qinglin, intending to make for Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Que tou, with garrison commander Xue Bozhen and several thousand men, he marched on foot toward Qinglin, aiming for Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 夜止山間宿，殺馬勞將士。

translations.literal: At night he halted to camp in the hills and slaughtered horses to refresh the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: That night he camped in the hills and slaughtered horses to feed his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 顗顧伯珍曰：「我舉八州以謀王室，未一戰而散，豈非天邪。

translations.literal: Yan turned to Bozhen and said, "I raised eight provinces to serve the royal house, yet before one battle we scattered—is this not Heaven's will?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan turned to Bozhen and said, "I mobilized eight provinces for the throne, yet we broke before a single battle—is this not Heaven's will?"

sentences.zh: 非不能死，豈欲草間求活，望一至尋陽，謝罪主上，然後自刎耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I cannot die; I do not wish to live like grass in the wild. I hope only to reach Xunyang, confess guilt before the sovereign, and then cut my own throat.
translations.idiomatic: I could die, but I will not crawl through the weeds for life. I mean only to reach Xunyang, confess before the throne, and then fall on my sword.

sentences.zh: 」因慷慨叱左右索節，無復應者。

translations.literal: He then spoke passionately and shouted for his attendants to bring his staff of office; none answered.
translations.idiomatic: He cried out passionately for his staff of office; no one responded.

sentences.zh: 及旦，伯珍請求間言，乃斬顗首詣錢溪馬軍主襄陽俞湛之降。

translations.literal: At dawn Bozhen asked to speak with him privately, then cut off Yan's head and went to surrender to Yu Zhizhi, cavalry commander at Qianxi in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Bozhen asked a private word, then cut off Yan's head and surrendered to Yu Zhizhi, cavalry commander at Qianxi in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 湛之因斬伯珍並送首以為己功。

translations.literal: Zhizhi then cut off Bozhen's head as well and sent both heads as his own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi then killed Bozhen too and sent both heads as proof of his own merit.

sentences.zh: 明帝忿顗違叛，流屍于江，弟子彖收瘞於石頭後岡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, angered at Yan's rebellion, cast his corpse into the river; his nephew Bian collected and buried it on the hill behind Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, furious at Yan's defection, had his body thrown into the river; his nephew Bian secretly gathered and buried him on the hill behind Shitou.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，方得改葬。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, proper reburial was at last permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Yan was at last given proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 顗子戩、昂。

translations.literal: Yan's sons Zhan and Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's sons Zhan and Ang.

sentences.zh: 戩為黃門侍郎，戍盆城。

translations.literal: Zhan was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and garrisoned Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and garrisoned Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 尋陽敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Xunyang fell, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunyang fell he was executed.

sentences.zh: 洵弟濯子 粲

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Zhuo's son Can
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Zhuo's son Can

sentences.zh: 粲字景倩，洵弟子也。

translations.literal: Can, styled Jingqian, was a son of Xun's younger brother Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Can, courtesy name Jingqian, was the son of Xun's younger brother Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 父濯，揚州秀才，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Zhuo, a provincial graduate of Yangzhou, died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuo, a Yangzhou provincial graduate, died young.

sentences.zh: 粲幼孤，祖哀之，名之曰湣孫。

translations.literal: Can was orphaned in infancy; his grandfather pitied him and named him Min Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Can lost his father in infancy; his grandfather pitied him and called him Min Sun.

sentences.zh: 伯叔並當世榮顯，而湣孫饑寒不足。

translations.literal: His uncles were all eminent in their generation, yet Min Sun knew hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles all rose to glory in their day, yet Min Sun still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 母琅邪王氏，太尉長史誕之女也。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Wang clan of Langye, daughter of Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant Dan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a Wang of Langye, daughter of Chief Clerk Dan to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 躬事績紡，以供朝夕。

translations.literal: She herself spun and wove to supply their daily needs.
translations.idiomatic: She spun and wove herself to meet their daily needs.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，復為侍中，領射聲校尉，封興平縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he was again made Palace Attendant and concurrently Commandant of the Archers' Guard, enfeoffed as Viscount of Xingping County.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 1 he again became Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Archers' Guard, enfeoffed as Viscount of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐納山陰人丁承文貨，舉為會稽郡孝廉，免官。

translations.literal: In the third year he was dismissed from office for accepting bribes from Ding Chengwen of Shanyin and recommending him as Filial and Incorrupt of Kuaiji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was removed for taking bribes from Ding Chengwen of Shanyin and recommending him as Filial and Incorrupt of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 五年，為左衛將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he became General of the Left Guard and was additionally made Chief of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became General of the Left Guard and was additionally made Chief of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉吏部尚書，左衛如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, retaining the Left Guard as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he became Director of the Ministry of Personnel while keeping the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 其年，皇太子冠，上臨宴東宮，與顏師伯、柳元景、沈慶之等並摴蒱，湣孫勸師伯酒，師伯不飲，湣孫因相裁辱曰：「不能與佞人周旋。

translations.literal: That year, at the crown prince's capping ceremony, the emperor attended a banquet in the Eastern Palace and played dice with Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanjing, Shen Qingzhi, and others; Min Sun urged Shibo to drink, but Shibo would not; Min Sun therefore insulted him, saying, "I cannot keep company with flatterers."
translations.idiomatic: That year, at the crown prince's coming-of-age feast, the emperor played dice with Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanjing, Shen Qingzhi, and others. Min Sun pressed Shibo to drink; when Shibo refused, Min Sun snapped, "I do not keep company with sycophants."

sentences.zh: 」師伯見寵于上，上常嫌湣孫以寒素陵之，因此發怒曰：「袁濯兒不逢朕，員外郎未可得也，而敢以寒士遇物！

translations.literal: Shibo was favored by the emperor, who often resented Min Sun's contempt toward him as a man of humble birth; he therefore flared in anger and said, "Had Yuan Zhuo's son not met me, he would never even have become an outer-office gentleman—and he dares treat a poor scholar this way!"
translations.idiomatic: Shibo enjoyed imperial favor, and the emperor already resented Min Sun's disdain for a man of low birth. He exploded: "Without me, Yuan Zhuo's son would never have risen even to outer-office gentleman—and he dares treat a poor scholar like this!"

sentences.zh: 」將手刃之，命引下席。

translations.literal: He was about to cut him down with his own hand and ordered him dragged from the seat.
translations.idiomatic: He nearly drew his blade on the spot and had Min Sun pulled from the table.

sentences.zh: 湣孫色不變，沈、柳並起謝，久之得釋。

translations.literal: Min Sun's color did not change; Shen and Liu both rose to apologize, and after a long while he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Min Sun's face never changed; Shen and Liu both rose to plead, and after a long while he was spared.

sentences.zh: 出為海陵太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as Administrator of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，湣孫在郡，夢日墮其胸上，因驚。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Min Sun was in his commandery and dreamed the sun fell onto his chest, and was startled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Min Sun was in his prefecture and dreamed the sun fell on his chest—then woke in alarm.

sentences.zh: 尋被徵管機密，歷吏部尚書，侍中，驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to manage confidential affairs, serving successively as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Palace Attendant, and General of the Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to handle confidential affairs, serving in turn as Director of Personnel, Palace Attendant, and General of the Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 湣孫峻于儀範，廢帝裸之迫使走，湣孫雅步如常，顧而言曰：「風雨如晦，雞鳴不已。

translations.literal: Min Sun was strict in ritual bearing; the Deposed Emperor stripped him naked and forced him to run, yet Min Sun walked with elegant step as usual and said as he went, "Wind and rain darken the sky, yet the cock crows without cease."
translations.idiomatic: Min Sun was punctilious in deportment; the Deposed Emperor stripped him and forced him to run, yet he walked with the same easy grace and quoted the Book of Songs: "Wind and rain darken the sky, yet the cock crows without cease."

sentences.zh: 」明帝泰始元年，為司徒左長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, he became Chief Clerk of the Left to the Minister of Education and Administrator of Eastern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 1 under Emperor Ming he became chief clerk of the left to the Minister of Education and Administrator of Eastern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 湣孫清整有風操，自遇甚高，嘗著妙德先生傳以續嵇康高士傳後以自況曰：「有妙德先生，陳國人也。

translations.literal: Min Sun was upright and possessed moral bearing; he thought highly of himself and once wrote A Biography of Master Miaode to follow Ji Kang's Biographies of High-Minded Men as a self-portrait, saying, "There was a Master Miaode, a man of Chen."
translations.idiomatic: Min Sun was austere and principled, with a high opinion of himself. He once wrote A Biography of Master Miaode, continuing Ji Kang's Biographies of High-Minded Men as self-portraiture: "There was a Master Miaode, a man of Chen."

sentences.zh: 氣志深虛，姿神清映，性孝履順，棲沖業簡，有舜之遺風。

translations.literal: His spirit was deep and empty, his bearing clear and luminous; filial in nature and orderly in conduct, he dwelt in humility and pursued simplicity, with the remnant wind of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit ran deep and clear, his bearing bright; dutiful and orderly, he lived in humility and plainness, with something of Shun's way about him.

sentences.zh: 先生幼夙多疾，性疏懶，無所營尚；

translations.literal: From youth the master had many illnesses and was by nature lax and lazy, with nothing he pursued or admired;
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was often ill, lax and idle, with no ambition he cared to pursue;

sentences.zh: 然九流百氏之言，雕龍談天之藝，皆泛識其大歸，而不以成名。

translations.literal: yet in the words of the nine streams and hundred schools, and in the arts of ornate rhetoric and celestial discourse, he broadly knew their general drift without making a name by them.
translations.idiomatic: yet of the nine schools and hundred authors, of ornate rhetoric and celestial disputation, he grasped the drift without making a name from any of it.

sentences.zh: 家貧嘗仕，非其好也。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he once took office, but it was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: Poverty once drove him into office, but office was not his love.

sentences.zh: 混其聲跡，晦其心用，席門常掩，三徑裁通。

translations.literal: He mingled his voice and tracks, hid his heart's use; his reed gate was always shut, and the three paths were barely open.
translations.idiomatic: He blurred his tracks and hid his intent; his reed gate stayed shut, the three paths barely trodden.

sentences.zh: 雖揚子寂漠，嚴叟沈冥，不是過也。

translations.literal: Though Yangzi was silent and remote and old Yan was deep in obscurity, he was no less than they.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong's silence and Yan Zun's obscurity were no greater than his.

sentences.zh: 修道遂志，終無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: Cultivating the Way and fulfilling his will, in the end he had no fame to be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated the Way and kept his purpose, yet in the end won no fame worth naming.

sentences.zh: 」又嘗謂周旋人曰：「昔有一國，國中一水號曰狂泉，國人飲此水無不狂，唯國君穿井而汲，獨得無恙。

translations.literal: He also once said to those around him, "In old times there was a state in which a stream called the Mad Spring flowed; all who drank it went mad, save the ruler, who dug his own well and alone remained whole."
translations.idiomatic: He also told his companions: "Once there was a country with a stream called Mad Spring. All who drank went mad—only the king, who dug his own well, stayed sane."

sentences.zh: 國人既並狂，反謂國主之不狂為狂，於是聚謀共執國主，療其狂疾。

translations.literal: When the people had all gone mad, they instead said the ruler's sanity was madness, and so gathered to seize the king and cure his mad sickness.
translations.idiomatic: When the whole country was mad, they decided the king's sanity was madness and seized him to cure it.

sentences.zh: 火艾針藥，莫不必具，國主不任其苦，於是到泉所酌水飲之，飲畢便狂，君臣大小其狂若一，眾乃歡然。

translations.literal: Fire, moxa, needles, and drugs were all prepared without fail; the king could not bear the pain, so he went to the spring, drank, and at once went mad; ruler and subjects, great and small, were mad alike, and all rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: Fire, moxa, needles, and drugs were readied; the king could not endure the treatment, drank from the spring, and at once went mad. Ruler and people alike were mad, and all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 我既不狂，難以獨立，比亦欲試飲此水矣。」

translations.literal: I am not mad and cannot stand alone; I too mean to try drinking this water."
translations.idiomatic: I am not mad and cannot stand alone—I too mean to try that water."

sentences.zh: 幼慕荀奉倩為人，孝武時求改名粲，不許，至明帝立，乃請改為粲，字景倩。

translations.literal: From youth he admired Xun Fengqian's character; in Emperor Xiaowu's time he asked to change his name to Can, but was refused; only when Emperor Ming took the throne did he obtain the change to Can, styled Jingqian.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he admired Xun Fengqian; under Emperor Xiaowu he asked to rename himself Can and was refused; only when Emperor Ming succeeded did he become Can, courtesy name Jingqian.

sentences.zh: 其外孫王筠又云：「明帝多忌諱，反語袁湣為『殞門』，帝意惡之，乃令改焉。

translations.literal: His grandson by a daughter, Wang Yun, also said, "Emperor Ming had many taboos; in reverse speech Yuan Min became 'Gate of Death,' which the emperor hated, and so he ordered the change."
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Wang Yun also said Emperor Ming hated taboo wordplay—Yuan Min reversed sounded like "Gate of Death"—and ordered the change for that reason.

sentences.zh: 」二年，遷領軍將軍，仗士三十人入六門。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Commander of the Palace Guard, with thirty armed retainers entering the Six Gates.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became Commander of the Palace Guard, with thirty armed retainers admitted through the Six Gates.

sentences.zh: 其年，徙中書令，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: That year he was moved to Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became Director of the Palace Secretariat and Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉尚書僕射，尋領吏部。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon also directed the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon also directed Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年，加中書令，又領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was additionally made Director of the Palace Secretariat and also Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he additionally became Director of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 粲負才尚氣，愛好虛遠，雖位任隆重，不以事務經懷。

translations.literal: Can relied on talent and prized spirit, loving what was lofty and remote; though his rank and duties were weighty, he did not let affairs weigh on his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Can trusted in talent and temperament, loving what was lofty and far; though his posts were weighty, business never burdened his mind.

sentences.zh: 獨步園林，詩酒自適。

translations.literal: Alone he walked the garden groves, finding his ease in wine and verse.
translations.idiomatic: Alone in the gardens he found ease in wine and poetry.

sentences.zh: 家居負郭，每杖策逍遙，當其意得，悠然忘反。

translations.literal: His home lay outside the city wall; leaning on his staff he wandered at will, and when his mood was satisfied he forgot to return.
translations.idiomatic: His house stood just beyond the walls; staff in hand he wandered at will and, when content, forgot to come home.

sentences.zh: 郡南一家頗有竹石，粲率爾步往，亦不通主人，直造竹所，嘯詠自得。

translations.literal: South of the commandery one household had fine bamboo and rock; Can strode there on impulse, without notifying the host, and went straight to the bamboo grove, whistling and reciting in self-contentment.
translations.idiomatic: South of the prefecture one house had fine bamboo and stone; Can walked there on impulse, never announcing himself, and went straight to the bamboo to whistle and recite in contentment.

sentences.zh: 主人出，語笑款然。

translations.literal: The host came out and they talked and laughed with easy warmth.
translations.idiomatic: The owner came out; they talked and laughed with easy warmth.

sentences.zh: 俄而車騎羽儀並至門，方知是袁尹。

translations.literal: Presently carriage guards and insignia arrived at the gate together, and only then did they know it was Prefect Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon carriage escorts and insignia arrived at the gate—only then did they learn he was Prefect Yuan.

sentences.zh: 又嘗步屧白楊郊野間，道遇一士大夫，便呼與酣飲，明日此人謂被知顧，到門求進。

translations.literal: Another time, walking in sandals through the white poplar fields beyond the city, he met a gentleman on the road, called him to drink deeply, and the next day the man, thinking himself singled out for favor, came to his gate seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Once, walking in sandals through poplar fields beyond the walls, he met a gentleman and called him to drink; the next day the man, thinking himself noticed, came seeking favor.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「昨飲酒無偶，聊相要耳。

translations.literal: Can said, "Yesterday I had no companion for wine and merely invited you for company."
translations.idiomatic: Can said, "Yesterday I lacked a drinking companion and merely asked you along."

sentences.zh: 」竟不與相見。

translations.literal: In the end he would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He never received him.

sentences.zh: 嘗作五言詩，言：「訪跡雖中宇，循寄乃滄洲」。

translations.literal: He once composed a pentasyllabic poem saying, "I seek traces within the central realm, yet my heart lodges on the blue isles."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a pentasyllabic line: "I walk the heartland's paths, yet my heart dwells on blue isles."

sentences.zh: 蓋其志也。

translations.literal: Such was his intent.
translations.idiomatic: That was his intent.

sentences.zh: 二年，桂陽王休範為逆，粲扶曳入殿，詔加兵自隨，府置佐吏。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince of Guiyang Xiufan rebelled; Can, leaning on attendants, entered the hall; an edict added armed guards at his side and set up staff officers in his office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled; Can, leaning on attendants, entered the hall; an edict added armed guards and staff officers to his office.

sentences.zh: 時兵難危急，賊已至南掖門，諸將意沮，咸莫能奮。

translations.literal: At that time the military crisis was dire; the rebels had already reached the Southern Wing Gate, and the generals' spirits were dampened—none could rouse themselves to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis was acute: rebels had reached the Southern Wing Gate, spirits among the generals sank, and none could stir to fight.

sentences.zh: 粲慷慨謂諸將帥曰：「寇賊已逼，而眾情離阻，孤子受先帝顧托，本以死報，今日當與褚護軍同死社稷。

translations.literal: Can spoke passionately to the commanders, saying, "The bandits are already upon us and the men's hearts are divided and blocked; I received the late emperor's trust and originally meant to repay him with death—today I shall die for the state together with Protector-General Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Can spoke fiercely to the commanders: "The enemy is at the gate and hearts are divided. The late emperor entrusted me; today I die for the realm with Protector-General Chu."

sentences.zh: 」因命左右被馬，辭色哀壯。

translations.literal: He then ordered his attendants to saddle horses; his bearing was mournful and stern.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered horses saddled; his face was grief-stricken and resolute.

sentences.zh: 於是陳顯達等感激出戰，賊即平殄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Xianda and others, stirred, went out to battle, and the rebels were at once destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda and others, stirred, went out to fight and the rebels were crushed at once.

sentences.zh: 事寧，授中書監，即本號開府儀同三司，領司徒。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, and with his existing title made Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Cord, concurrently Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Cord, and concurrently Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 以揚州解為府，固不肯移。

translations.literal: Because Yangzhou was dissolved to form his office, he firmly refused to move.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou was dissolved to form his office, but he firmly refused to relocate.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙尚書令，衛軍、開府如故，並固辭，服終乃受命。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing, retaining Guard Commander and Grand Master as before, again firmly declining until mourning ended before accepting.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was offered Director of the Masters of Writing with Guard Commander and Grand Master unchanged; he declined until mourning ended, then accepted.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，進爵為侯，又不受。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and promoted in rank to marquis, but again would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and promoted to marquis, but again refused.

sentences.zh: 時齊高帝方革命，粲自以身受顧托，不欲事二姓，密有異圖。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi founding emperor was in the midst of revolution; Can, because he had received the late emperor's trust, did not wish to serve two dynasties and secretly harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi founder was seizing power; Can, having received the late emperor's trust, would not serve two houses and secretly plotted otherwise.

sentences.zh: 劉彥節宋氏宗室，前湘州刺史王蘊太后兄子，素好武事，並慮不見容于齊高帝，皆與粲結，諸將帥黃回、任候伯、孫曇瓘、王宜興、彭文之、卜伯興等並與粲合。

translations.literal: Liu Yanjie of the Song imperial clan, and Wang Yun, elder son of the Empress Dowager's brother and former Inspector of Xiangzhou, both loved military affairs and feared they would not be tolerated by the Qi founder; they all joined with Can, and the commanders Huang Hui, Ren Houbo, Sun Tanjuan, Wang Yixing, Peng Wenzhi, Bu Boxing, and others all united with Can.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanjie of Song's imperial clan and Wang Yun, the empress dowager's nephew and former Xiangzhou inspector, both martial men, feared the Qi founder would not spare them; they joined Can, along with commanders Huang Hui, Ren Houbo, Sun Tanjuan, Wang Yixing, Peng Wenzhi, Bu Boxing, and others.

sentences.zh: 升明元年，荊州刺史沈攸之舉兵反，齊高帝自詣粲，粲稱疾不見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming, Inspector of Jingzhou Shen Youzhi raised troops in rebellion; the Qi founder came in person to Can, but Can pleaded illness and would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 1 Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; the Qi founder came to Can in person, but Can pleaded illness and refused audience.

sentences.zh: 粲宗人袁達以為不宜示異同。

translations.literal: Can's clansman Yuan Da thought he should not show difference of intent.
translations.idiomatic: Can's kinsman Yuan Da thought he should not reveal dissent.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「彼若劫我入台，便無辭以拒，一如此，不復得出矣。

translations.literal: Can said, "If they force me into the palace, I shall have no excuse to refuse; once that happens, I can never get out again."
translations.idiomatic: Can said, "If they drag me into the palace I cannot refuse; once inside, I never get out again."

sentences.zh: 」時齊高帝入屯朝堂，彥節從父弟領軍將軍韞入直門下省，卜伯興為直合，黃回諸將皆率軍出新亭。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi founder entered and encamped in the Court Hall; Yanjie's younger cousin by father's side, Commander of the Palace Guard Yun, entered duty in the Gate Down Office; Bu Boxing was on gate duty; Huang Hui and the other generals all led armies out to Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi founder encamped in the Court Hall; Yanjie's cousin Yun, Commander of the Palace Guard, entered duty at the Gate Down Office; Bu Boxing held gate duty; Huang Hui and the rest led troops to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 粲克日謀矯太后令，使韞、伯興率宿衛兵攻齊高帝於朝堂，回率軍來應，彥節、候伯等並赴石頭。

translations.literal: Can set a date to forge a command from the empress dowager, ordering Yun and Boxing to lead the palace guard against the Qi founder in the Court Hall, while Hui would lead troops to respond and Yanjie, Houbo, and the others would all go to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Can set a date to forge an empress dowager's order: Yun and Boxing would strike the Qi founder in the Court Hall with palace guards, Hui would respond with troops, and Yanjie, Houbo, and the rest would rush Shitou.

sentences.zh: 事泄。

translations.literal: The plot leaked.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊高帝遣將薛深、蘇烈、王天生等領兵戍石頭，云以助粲，實禦之也。

translations.literal: Earlier the Qi founder had sent the generals Xue Shen, Su Lie, Wang Tiansheng, and others to garrison Shitou, saying it was to assist Can but in fact to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Qi founder had sent Xue Shen, Su Lie, Wang Tiansheng, and others to garrison Shitou, claiming to aid Can but in truth to contain him.

sentences.zh: 又令腹心王敬則為直合，與伯興共總禁兵。

translations.literal: He also placed his trusted man Wang Jingze on gate duty to share command of the forbidden troops with Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: He also put his confidant Wang Jingze on gate duty to share forbidden-troop command with Boxing.

sentences.zh: 王蘊聞彥節已奔，歎曰：「今年事敗矣。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, hearing Yanjie had already fled, sighed and said, "This year's affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, hearing Yanjie had fled, sighed, "This year the cause is lost."

sentences.zh: 」乃狼狽率部曲向石頭，薛深等據門射之。

translations.literal: He then hurriedly led his followers toward Shitou; Xue Shen and the others held the gate and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried toward Shitou with his followers; Xue Shen and the others held the gate and shot.

sentences.zh: 蘊謂粲已敗，乃便散走。

translations.literal: Yun thought Can had already been defeated and at once scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yun thought Can had already fallen and at once broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝以報敬則，敬則誅韞並伯興，又遣軍主戴僧靜向石頭助薛深自倉門入。

translations.literal: The Qi founder reported to Jingze; Jingze executed Yun and Boxing, and also sent the army commander Dai Sengjing toward Shitou to aid Xue Shen entering through the granary gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi founder informed Jingze; Jingze killed Yun and Boxing and sent Dai Sengjing to Shitou to aid Xue Shen through the granary gate.

sentences.zh: 時粲與彥節等列兵登東門，僧靜分兵攻府西門，彥節與兒踰城出。

translations.literal: At that time Can and Yanjie and the others drew up troops and mounted the East Gate; Sengjing divided his force to attack the west gate of the residence; Yanjie and his son climbed over the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Can and Yanjie drew up troops on the East Gate; Sengjing split force to hit the residence's west gate; Yanjie and his son went over the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 粲還坐，列燭自照，謂其子最曰：「本知一木不能止大廈之崩，但以名義至此耳。

translations.literal: Can returned and sat down, set out candles to light himself, and said to his son Zui, "I always knew one timber cannot halt a great hall's collapse, but I came this far only for the sake of the name of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Can returned, lit candles, and told his son Zui, "I always knew one timber cannot stop a hall from falling—but I came this far for the name of righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」僧靜挺身暗往，奮刀直前欲斬之。

translations.literal: Sengjing advanced in the dark, drew his blade, and rushed straight forward intending to cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Sengjing stole forward in the dark, blade raised, intending to cut him down.

sentences.zh: 子最覺有異，大叫抱父乞先死，兵士人人莫不隕涕。

translations.literal: Zui sensed something amiss, cried out loudly, and clung to his father begging to die first; the soldiers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zui sensed danger, cried out, and clung to his father begging to die first; the soldiers wept.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「我不失忠臣，汝不失孝子。

translations.literal: Can said, "I shall not fail as a loyal minister; you shall not fail as a filial son."
translations.idiomatic: Can said, "I keep faith as a loyal minister; you keep faith as a filial son."

sentences.zh: 」仍求筆作啟云：「臣義奉大宋，策名兩畢，今便歸魂墳壟，永就山丘。

translations.literal: He then asked for a brush and wrote a memorial saying, "Your servant rightfully served great Song, pledged his name twice over; now I return my soul to the mound and forever go to the hill."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for brush and wrote: "I served great Song and pledged my name twice; now I return my soul to the mound and go forever to the hills."

sentences.zh: 」僧靜乃並斬之。

translations.literal: Sengjing then cut them both down.
translations.idiomatic: Sengjing then killed them both.

sentences.zh: 初，粲大明中與蕭惠開、周朗同車行，逢大珩開駐車，惠開自照鏡曰：「無年可仕。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Daming era Can rode in the same carriage with Xiao Huike and Zhou Lang; they met a great rainbow and Huike stopped the carriage; Huike looked in the mirror and said, "No years left for office."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Daming, Can rode with Xiao Huike and Zhou Lang; a great rainbow appeared and Huike stopped the carriage, looked in a mirror, and said, "No years left for office."

sentences.zh: 」朗執鏡良久曰：「視死如歸。

translations.literal: Lang held the mirror long and said, "To look on death as going home."
translations.idiomatic: Lang held the mirror long and said, "To look on death as going home."

sentences.zh: 」粲最後曰：「當至三公而不終。

translations.literal: Can last said, "I shall reach the Three Dukes but not finish my term."
translations.idiomatic: Can last said, "I shall reach the Three Dukes but not finish my term."

sentences.zh: 」至是如言。

translations.literal: At this it came to pass as he said.
translations.idiomatic: At this it came to pass as he said.

sentences.zh: 粲子 最

translations.literal: Can's son Zui
translations.idiomatic: Can's son Zui

sentences.zh: 最字文高，時年十七，既父子俱殞，左右分散，任候伯等其夜並自新亭赴石頭，其後皆誅。

translations.literal: Zui, styled Wengao, was then seventeen; father and son both perished, attendants scattered, and Ren Houbo and the others that same night all went from Xinting to Shitou and were afterward executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zui, courtesy name Wengao, was seventeen; father and son both died, attendants scattered, and Ren Houbo and the rest went from Xinting to Shitou that night and were later executed.

sentences.zh: 粲小兒數歲，乳母將投粲門生狄靈慶。

translations.literal: Can's little son, a few years old, his wet nurse was about to take him to Can's student Di Lingqing.
translations.idiomatic: Can's little son, only a few years old, was being taken by his wet nurse to Can's student Di Lingqing.

sentences.zh: 靈慶曰：「吾聞出郎君者有厚賞，今袁氏已滅，汝匿之尚誰為乎？

translations.literal: Lingqing said, "I hear there is rich reward for whoever yields up the young master; now the Yuan clan is destroyed—whom do you hide him for?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingqing said, "I hear whoever yields up the young master gets rich reward; the Yuans are destroyed—whom do you hide him for?"

sentences.zh: 」遂抱以首。

translations.literal: He then carried the boy off by the head.
translations.idiomatic: He then carried the boy off by the head.

sentences.zh: 乳母號泣呼天曰：「公昔於汝有恩，故冒難歸汝，奈何欲殺郎君以求小利。

translations.literal: The wet nurse wailed to Heaven, saying, "Your lord once showed you kindness, so I risk death to bring him to you—how can you seek to kill the young master for petty gain?"
translations.idiomatic: The wet nurse wailed to Heaven: "Your lord once favored you, so I risk death to bring the boy—how can you kill him for petty gain?"

sentences.zh: 若天地鬼神有知，我見汝滅門。

translations.literal: If Heaven and earth and the ghosts have knowledge, I shall see your house destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven, earth, and the ghosts see, I shall watch your house destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」此兒死後，靈慶常見兒騎大寧毛狗戲如平常，經年餘，鬥場忽見一狗走入其家，遇靈慶於庭噬殺之，少時妻子皆沒。

translations.literal: After the child died, Lingqing often saw the boy riding the big black-furred dog and playing as usual; after more than a year, a dog suddenly ran into his house in the arena and killed Lingqing in the courtyard; soon wife and children all perished.
translations.idiomatic: After the child died, Lingqing often saw the boy riding the big black dog at play as before; more than a year later a dog ran into his house and killed him in the courtyard; soon wife and children perished.

sentences.zh: 此狗即袁郎所常騎者也。

translations.literal: This dog was the one young Master Yuan often rode.
translations.idiomatic: That dog was the one young Master Yuan often rode.

sentences.zh: 粲省事莫嗣祖，粲常所委信，與劉彥節等宣密謀。

translations.literal: Can's office aide Mo Sizu, whom Can always trusted, together with Liu Yanjie and others spread the secret plot.
translations.idiomatic: Can's office aide Mo Sizu, whom Can always trusted, helped spread the secret plot with Liu Yanjie and others.

sentences.zh: 至是齊高帝問曰：「汝知袁粲謀逆，何不啟？

translations.literal: At this the Qi founder asked, "You knew Yuan Can plotted rebellion—why did you not report it?"
translations.idiomatic: The Qi founder asked, "You knew Yuan Can plotted rebellion—why not report it?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣祖曰：「小人無識，曲蒙袁公厚恩，實不仰負，今日就死分甘。

translations.literal: Sizu said, "This petty man lacks understanding and was wrongly shown deep favor by Lord Yuan; I truly cannot face up to that debt; today to die is sweet portion."
translations.idiomatic: Sizu said, "I am a petty man who wrongly received Lord Yuan's deep favor; I cannot face that debt—death today is sweet portion."

sentences.zh: 官若賜性命，亦不忍背粲而獨生也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty grants life, I also cannot bear to live alone betraying Can.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty spares me, I still cannot live alone betraying Can.

sentences.zh: 」戴僧靜勸殺之。

translations.literal: Dai Sengjing urged that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing urged execution.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼各為其主。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Each served his own lord."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Each served his own lord."

sentences.zh: 」遂赦焉，用為省事。

translations.literal: He then pardoned him and employed him as office aide.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned him and kept him as office aide.

sentences.zh: 歷朝所賞。

translations.literal: He was rewarded through successive reigns.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded through successive reigns.

sentences.zh: 梁豫章王直新出合，中旨用嗣祖為師。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yuzhang Zhi of Liang first left the palace school, an imperial order appointed Sizu as his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Prince Zhi of Yuzhang first left the palace school, an imperial order made Sizu his tutor.

sentences.zh: 顗弟覬子 彖

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Ji's son Bian
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Ji's son Bian

sentences.zh: 彖字偉才，顗弟覬之子也。

translations.literal: Bian, styled Weicai, was the son of Yan's younger brother Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, courtesy name Weicai, was the son of Yan's younger brother Ji.

sentences.zh: 覬好學美才，早有清譽，仕宋位武陵內史。

translations.literal: Ji loved learning and had fine talent; from early he had a clear reputation and served Song as Internal Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Ji loved learning and had fine talent; early he won a clear name and served Song as Internal Administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 彖少有風氣，善屬文及談玄，舉秀才，歷諸王府參軍，不就。

translations.literal: Bian from youth had spirit and bearing, was skilled at composing prose and discussing the dark learning, was nominated as provincial graduate, served as staff officer in various princely households, but would not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Bian from youth had spirit, wrote well and debated dark learning, was nominated provincial graduate, served in princely households, but refused appointment.

sentences.zh: 覬臨終與兄顗書曰：「史公才識可喜，足懋先基矣。

translations.literal: When Ji was near death he wrote to his elder brother Yan, saying, "Historian Gong's talent and insight are pleasing; enough to honor the ancestral foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Near death Ji wrote his elder brother Yan: "Historian Gong's talent and insight are pleasing—enough to honor our house."

sentences.zh: 」史公，彖小字也。

translations.literal: Historian Gong was Bian's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Historian Gong was Bian's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 及顗見誅，宋明帝投屍江中，不許斂葬。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed, Emperor Ming of Song cast his corpse into the river and forbade burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was killed, Emperor Ming of Song cast his body into the river and forbade burial.

sentences.zh: 彖與舊奴一人，微服求屍，四十餘日乃得，密瘞石頭後岡，身自負土。

translations.literal: Bian, with one old servant, in plain clothes sought the corpse; after more than forty days he found it, secretly buried it on the hill behind Shitou, and himself carried earth.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, with one old servant in plain clothes, searched more than forty days for the body, secretly buried it on the hill behind Shitou, and carried earth himself.

sentences.zh: 懷其文集，未嘗離身。

translations.literal: He kept Ji's collected writings and never let them leave his person.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Ji's collected writings and never let them leave his side.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩後，乃改葬顗。

translations.literal: After Emperor Ming died he at last gave Yan proper reburial.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming's death he at last gave Yan proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 從叔司徒粲、祖舅征西將軍蔡興宗並器之。

translations.literal: His uncle by father's side, Minister of Education Can, and maternal uncle, General Who Conquers the West Cai Xingzong, both valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Can, Minister of Education, and maternal uncle Cai Xingzong, General Who Conquers the West, both valued him.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為齊高帝太傅相國主簿，秘書丞。

translations.literal: Serving Song he was Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor and Chancellor and Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he was chief clerk to the Grand Tutor and Chancellor and Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為中書郎，兼太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he was Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he was Director of the Palace Secretariat and Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 又以中書郎兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He also served as Director of the Palace Secretariat concurrently with Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He also doubled as Director of the Palace Secretariat and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 坐彈謝超宗簡奏依違，免官。

translations.literal: For impeaching Xie Chaozong with a memorial that was evasive, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed for impeaching Xie Chaozong in a memorial that hedged its charges.

sentences.zh: 後拜廬陵王諮議。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Adviser to the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Adviser to the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 時南郡江陵縣人苟蔣之弟胡之婦為曾口寺沙門所淫，夜入苟家，蔣之殺沙門，為官司所檢，蔣之列家門穢行，欲告則恥，欲忍則不可，實己所殺，胡之列又如此，兄弟爭死。

translations.literal: At that time in Jiangling County of Nan Commandery, the wife of Hu Zhi, younger brother of Jiang Zhi, was violated by a monk of Zengkou Temple who entered the Jiang house by night; Jiang killed the monk and was investigated by the law offices; Jiang listed the family's shameful conduct, wishing to report yet ashamed, wishing to endure yet unable, for in truth he himself had killed the man, while Hu's memorial likewise said so—the brothers contended to die.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangling of Nan Commandery, Hu Zhi's wife was violated by a monk of Zengkou Temple who entered the Jiang house by night. Jiang killed the monk and was investigated; torn between reporting the family's shame and enduring silence, each brother claimed the killing and contended to die.

sentences.zh: 江陵令宗躬啟州，荊州刺史廬江王求博議。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jiangling Zong Gong reported to the province; the Inspector, Prince of Lujiang, sought broad deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling Magistrate Zong Gong reported to the province; the Inspector, Prince of Lujiang, sought broad deliberation.

sentences.zh: 彖曰：「夫迅寒急節，乃見松筠之操，危機迥構，方識貞孤之風。

translations.literal: Bian said, "In sudden cold and urgent season one sees the pine and bamboo's constancy; in crisis sharply built one knows the wind of steadfast solitude."
translations.idiomatic: Bian wrote: "Sudden cold reveals pine and bamboo; crisis reveals steadfast solitude."

sentences.zh: 竊以蔣之、胡之殺人，原心非暴，辯讞之日，友于讓生，事憐左右，義哀行路。

translations.literal: I hold that Jiang Zhi and Hu Zhi killed a man whose original intent was not violent; on the day of judgment brothers yielded life to each other—the affair moves those at hand and moves pity in passersby.
translations.idiomatic: I hold Jiang and Hu killed without original violence; at judgment each brother yielded life to the other—the case moved all who heard it.

sentences.zh: 昔文舉引謗，獲漏疏網，蔣之心跡，同符古人，若陷以深刑，實傷為善。

translations.literal: In old times Wen Ju cited slander and escaped the loose net; Jiang's heart and tracks accord with the ancients—if he is sunk in deep punishment, it truly wounds those who do good.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wen Ju escaped the loose net through cited slander; Jiang's heart and conduct match the ancients—deep punishment would wound the good.

sentences.zh: 」由是蔣之兄弟免死。

translations.literal: From this the Jiang brothers were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang brothers were spared death.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中庶子，出為冠軍將軍，監吳興郡事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and sent out as General Who Conquers the Champions and overseer of Wu Commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, then went out as General Who Conquers the Champions overseeing Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 彖性剛固以微言忤武帝，又薄王晏為人，晏請交不答。

translations.literal: Bian was by nature rigid and firm; subtle words offended Emperor Wu, and he also looked down on Wang Yan's character; when Yan asked for friendship he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was rigid by nature; subtle remarks offended Emperor Wu, and he scorned Wang Yan—when Yan sought friendship he refused.

sentences.zh: 武帝在便殿用金柄刀子翦瓜，晏在側曰：「外聞有金刀之言，恐不宜用此物。

translations.literal: The emperor in the side hall used a gold-handled knife to cut melon; Yan at his side said, "Outside there is talk of a golden blade—perhaps this object should not be used."
translations.idiomatic: In the side hall the emperor cut melon with a gold-handled knife; Yan at his side said, "Outside there is talk of a golden blade—perhaps this object should not be used."

sentences.zh: 」帝窮問所以，晏曰：「袁彖為臣說之。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed for the reason; Yan said, "Yuan Bian told me as his minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed for the reason; Yan said, "Yuan Bian told me as his minister."

sentences.zh: 」上銜怒良久。

translations.literal: The emperor harbored anger for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nursed anger for a long while.

sentences.zh: 彖到郡，坐過用祿錢，免官付東冶。

translations.literal: When Bian reached his commandery he was dismissed for overspending salary funds and sent to the eastern works.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian reached his commandery he was removed for overspending salary funds and sent to the eastern works prison.

sentences.zh: 彖妹為竟陵王子良妃，子良世子昭胄時年八歲，見武帝而形容慘悴，帝問其故，昭胄流涕曰：「臣舅負罪，今在尚方，臣母悲泣不食已積日，臣所以不寧。

translations.literal: Bian's younger sister was wife to Prince of Jingling Ziliang; Ziliang's heir Zhaozhou was then eight years old; seeing Emperor Wu his appearance was haggard; the emperor asked the reason; Zhaozhou wept and said, "My uncle bears guilt and is now in the Directorate; my mother weeps and will not eat—many days already—so I am unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Bian's sister was wife to Prince Ziliang of Jingling; heir Zhaozhou, eight, looked haggard before Emperor Wu and wept: "My uncle is imprisoned in the Directorate; my mother will not eat for days—I am unsettled."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「特為兒赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Specially for the boy's sake I pardon him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For the boy's sake alone I pardon him."

sentences.zh: 」既而帝游孫陵，望東冶，曰：「冶中有一好貴囚。

translations.literal: Presently the emperor toured Sunling, gazed toward the eastern works, and said, "In the works there is one fine noble prisoner."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor toured Sunling, looked toward the eastern works, and said, "In the works there is one fine noble prisoner."

sentences.zh: 」數日，與朝臣幸冶，履行庫藏，因宴飲，賜囚徒酒肉，敕見彖與語，明日釋之。

translations.literal: Several days later, with court ministers he visited the works, walked through the storehouses, and there feasted, giving wine and meat to the convicts; he ordered Bian seen and spoken with, and the next day released him.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he visited the works with court ministers, toured the storehouses, feasted, gave wine and meat to convicts, spoke with Bian, and released him the next day.

sentences.zh: 後為侍中。

translations.literal: Later he became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彖充腴異眾，每從射雉郊野，數人推扶，乃能徒步。

translations.literal: Bian was corpulent beyond the common run; whenever he followed the hunt for pheasants in the suburbs, several men had to support him before he could walk.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was unusually stout; on pheasant hunts in the suburbs several men had to support him before he could walk.

sentences.zh: 幼而母卒，養于伯母王氏，事之如親，閨門孝義。

translations.literal: His mother died when he was young and he was raised by his aunt, Lady Wang; he served her as kin; filial duty within the household.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died young and his aunt Lady Wang raised him; he served her as a parent—the household knew filial duty.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年卒，諡靖子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he died, posthumous title Viscount Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang 1 he died, posthumous title Viscount Jing.

sentences.zh: 彖宗人廓之，字思度，宏之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Bian's clansman Kuozhi, styled Sidu, was great-grandson of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's kinsman Kuozhi, courtesy name Sidu, was great-grandson of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 父景雋，宋世為淮南太守，以非罪見誅。

translations.literal: His father Jingjuan served Song as Administrator of Huainan and was executed for a non-capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingjuan served Song as Administrator of Huainan and was executed for a non-capital offense.

sentences.zh: 廓之終身不聽音樂，布衣蔬食，足不出門，示不臣于宋，時人以比晉之王裒。

translations.literal: Kuozhi all his life would not listen to music, ate plain food in coarse cloth, and never stepped outside his gate, showing he would not serve Song; contemporaries compared him to Wang Pou of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Kuozhi never listened to music, ate plain food in coarse cloth, never left his gate—refusing Song; men compared him to Jin's Wang Pou.

sentences.zh: 顏延之見其幼時，歎曰：「有子如袁廓足矣。

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi, seeing him as a child, sighed and said, "To have a son like Yuan Kuozhi is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi, seeing him as a child, sighed, "A son like Yuan Kuozhi is enough."

sentences.zh: 」齊國建，方出仕，稍至殿中郎，王儉、柳世隆傾心待之。

translations.literal: When Qi was established he at last entered service, gradually reaching Palace Gentleman; Wang Jian and Liu Shilong treated him with full regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was founded he at last entered service, rising to Palace Gentleman; Wang Jian and Liu Shilong treated him with full regard.

sentences.zh: 為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He became Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 于時何間亦稱才子，為文惠太子作楊畔歌，辭甚側麗，太子甚悅。

translations.literal: At that time He Jian was also called a talented man; he composed the Yangpan Song for Crown Prince Wenhuai, with language very tender and lovely, and the crown prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian was also called a talent; he wrote the Yangpan Song for Crown Prince Wenhuai in tender, lovely language, and the crown prince was delighted.

sentences.zh: 廓之諫曰：「夫楊畔者，既非典雅，而聲甚哀思，殿下當降意簫韶，奈何聽亡國之響。

translations.literal: Kuozhi remonstrated, saying, "Yangpan is neither elegant nor classical, and its tone is very mournful—Your Highness should incline to the music of Shun and Shao; how can you listen to the sound of a perishing state?"
translations.idiomatic: Kuozhi remonstrated: "Yangpan is neither elegant nor classical, and its tone is mournful—Your Highness should incline to the music of Shun and Shao, not the sound of a dying state."

sentences.zh: 」太子改容謝之。

translations.literal: The crown prince changed expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince changed expression and apologized.

sentences.zh: 顗子 昂

translations.literal: Yan's son Ang
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Ang

sentences.zh: 昂字千里，雍州刺史顗之子也，顗敗，藏於沙門。

translations.literal: Ang, styled Qianli, was son of Yan, Inspector of Yongzhou; when Yan was defeated he was hidden among monks.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, courtesy name Qianli, was son of Yan, Inspector of Yongzhou; when Yan fell he was hidden among monks.

sentences.zh: 沙門將以出關，關吏疑非常人，沙門杖而語之，遂免。

translations.literal: The monk was about to take him through the pass; the gate officer suspected he was no ordinary person; the monk beat him and spoke to him, and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A monk meant to take him through the pass; the gate officer suspected an extraordinary person; the monk beat him and coached his speech, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 或云：顗敗時，昂年五歲，乳媼攜抱匿於廬山，州郡於野求之，於乳媼匿所見一彪，因去，遂免。

translations.literal: Some say: when Yan was defeated Ang was five years old; his nurse carried and hid him on Mount Lu; the commandery and province searched the wilds; at the nurse's hiding place they saw a tiger and departed, and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Some say when Yan fell Ang was five; his nurse hid him on Mount Lu; searchers saw a tiger at the hiding place and withdrew, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 會赦得出，猶徙晉安。

translations.literal: When amnesty came he was released but still exiled to Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty freed him, but he was still exiled to Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 在南唯勤學，至元徽中聽還，時年十五。

translations.literal: In the south he studied diligently alone; in the Yuanhui era he was permitted to return, then aged fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the south he studied hard alone; in the Yuanhui era he was allowed to return, aged fifteen.

sentences.zh: 初顗敗傳首建鄴，藏於武庫，以漆題顗名以為志，至是始還之。

translations.literal: When Yan was defeated his head was sent to Jiankang and stored in the arsenal; lacquer inscribed Yan's name as a marker; only now was it returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell his head was sent to Jiankang and kept in the arsenal, lacquer inscribed with Yan's name as marker—only now was it returned.

sentences.zh: 昂號慟嘔血，絕而復蘇，以淚洗所題漆字皆滅，人以為孝感。

translations.literal: Ang wailed and vomited blood, fainting and reviving; with tears he washed the lacquer inscription and all the characters vanished—men took it as filial response.
translations.idiomatic: Ang wailed until he vomited blood, fainting and reviving; tears washed the lacquer inscription until every character vanished—men called it filial wonder.

sentences.zh: 葬訖，更制服廬於墓次，從兄彖常撫視抑譬之。

translations.literal: After burial he again donned mourning garments and built a hut at the tomb; his cousin Bian often came to comfort and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he donned mourning again and built a hut at the tomb; cousin Bian often came to comfort and restrain him.

sentences.zh: 昂容質修偉，冠絕人倫，以父亡不以理，終身不聽音樂。

translations.literal: Ang's bearing and stature were tall and fine, surpassing others; because his father's death was not by right principle, all his life he would not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's bearing was tall and fine, surpassing others; because his father's death was unjust, he never listened to music all his life.

sentences.zh: 後與彖同見從叔司徒粲，粲謂彖曰：「昂幼孤而能至此，故知名器自有所在。

translations.literal: Later he and Bian together saw their uncle by father's side, Minister of Education Can; Can said to Bian, "Ang, orphaned young, could come this far—so fame and vessel have their appointed place."
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Bian saw their uncle Can, Minister of Education; Can told Bian, "Ang, orphaned young, came this far—fame and office have their appointed place."

sentences.zh: 」仕齊為王儉鎮軍府功曹史。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he was Clerk on Wang Jian's Pacifying Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he was clerk on Wang Jian's Pacifying Army staff.

sentences.zh: 儉後為丹陽尹，於後堂獨引見昂，指北堂謂曰：「卿必居此。

translations.literal: Jian later became Prefect of Danyang; in the rear hall he received Ang alone and, pointing to the north hall, said, "You shall dwell here."
translations.idiomatic: Jian later became Prefect of Danyang; in the rear hall he received Ang alone, pointed to the north hall, and said, "You shall dwell here."

sentences.zh: 」累遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 昂本名千里，齊永明中，武帝謂曰：「昂昂千里之駒，在卿有之。

translations.literal: Ang's original name was Qianli; in the Yongming era Emperor Wu said to him, "'Ang ang, a thousand-li colt'—in you it exists."
translations.idiomatic: Ang's original name was Qianli; in Yongming Emperor Wu told him, "'Ang ang, a thousand-li colt'—that is you."

sentences.zh: 今改卿名為昂，即字千里。

translations.literal: Now I change your name to Ang, and your style to Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: Now I change your name to Ang and your style to Qianli.

sentences.zh: 」後為衛軍武陵王長史。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Clerk to Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過禮，服未除而從兄彖卒。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended, before the mourning period was over his cousin Bian died.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother, before the period ended his cousin Bian died.

sentences.zh: 昂幼孤，為彖所養，乃制期服。

translations.literal: Ang was orphaned young and raised by Bian, and therefore observed one-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, orphaned young and raised by Bian, therefore observed one-year mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 人有怪而問之，昂致書以喻之曰：

translations.literal: Some found it strange and questioned him; Ang wrote in reply to explain, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Some found it strange and questioned him; Ang wrote to explain:

sentences.zh: 竊聞禮由恩斷，服以情申，故小功他邦，加制一等，同爨有緦，明之典籍。

translations.literal: I have heard that ritual is cut by affection and garments are extended by feeling; thus for lesser mourning in another state one adds a degree, and for those sharing the hearth there is the hemp of the closest tie—the classics make this clear.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard ritual follows affection and garments follow feeling: lesser mourning abroad adds a degree; those sharing a hearth wear the closest hemp—the classics say so.

sentences.zh: 孤子夙以不天，幼傾幹蔭，資敬未奉，過庭莫承，藐藐沖年，未達朱紫。
