translations.literal: I, orphaned, early lost Heaven's protection; in tender years I lost shelter; I never offered daily reverence, never received instruction in the hall; in tiny, distant years I did not yet know scarlet from purple.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, I lost Heaven's shelter; in tender years I never offered daily reverence or received hall instruction; in tiny years I did not know scarlet from purple.

sentences.zh: 從兄提養訓教，示以義方，每假其談價，虛其聲譽，得及人次，實亦有由。

translations.literal: My cousin raised, taught, and showed me the way of righteousness; he often lent me his reputation and borrowed me his voice, so that I could stand among men—truly there was cause.
translations.idiomatic: My cousin raised, taught, and showed me righteousness; he lent me reputation and voice so I could stand among men—there was real cause.

sentences.zh: 兼開拓房宇，處以華曠，同財共有，恣其取足，爾來三十餘年。

translations.literal: He also opened rooms and housed me in spacious brightness; we shared property and had common wealth, letting me take what I needed—for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He opened rooms and housed me in spacious brightness; we shared property and wealth, letting me take what I needed—for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 憐愛之至，言無異色，姊妹孤侄，成就一時。

translations.literal: Love to the utmost spoke without change of countenance; orphaned sisters and nephews he brought to completion in one time.
translations.idiomatic: Love to the utmost never changed his face; orphaned sisters and nephews he brought through in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 篤念之深，在終彌固，此恩此愛，畢壤不追。

translations.literal: Deep remembrance to the end grew ever firmer—such grace, such love, not even equal earth can repay.
translations.idiomatic: Deep remembrance grew ever firmer to the end—such grace, such love, not even earth can repay.

sentences.zh: 既情若同生，而服為諸從，言心即事，實未忍安。

translations.literal: Since feeling was like shared birth yet garments were those of a cousin, in heart and in fact I truly could not rest easy.
translations.idiomatic: Since feeling was like shared birth yet garments were those of a cousin, in heart and fact I could not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 昔馬棱與從弟毅同居，毅亡，棱為心服三年。

translations.literal: In old times Ma Ling lived with his younger cousin Yi; when Yi died, Ling wore heart-mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ma Ling lived with cousin Yi; when Yi died, Ling wore heart-mourning three years.

sentences.zh: 由也之不除喪，亦緣情而致制。

translations.literal: Zeng Shen's not leaving mourning also came from feeling and led to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen's not leaving mourning also came from feeling and led to regulation.

sentences.zh: 雖識不及古，誠懷感慕。

translations.literal: Though my understanding does not reach antiquity, my sincerity truly feels and admires.
translations.idiomatic: Though my understanding does not reach antiquity, my sincerity truly feels and admires.

sentences.zh: 常願千秋之後，從服期齊；

translations.literal: I always wished that after a thousand autumns my mourning might equal his in term;
translations.idiomatic: I always wished that after a thousand autumns my mourning might equal his in term;

sentences.zh: 不圖門衰禍集，一旦草土，殘息復罹今酷。

translations.literal: I never thought the gate's decline would gather calamity, and suddenly upon the grass and soil this surviving breath again met today's bitter blow.
translations.idiomatic: I never thought the house would decline into calamity, and suddenly upon the grave this surviving breath met today's bitter blow.

sentences.zh: 尋惟慟絕，彌劇彌深。

translations.literal: Searching my grief I nearly died; the pain grew ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: Searching my grief I nearly died; the pain grew ever keener.

sentences.zh: 今以餘喘，欲遂素志，庶寄其罔慕之痛，少伸無已之情。

translations.literal: Now with what breath remains I wish to fulfill my plain intent, hoping to lodge my boundless longing and slightly extend my unending feeling.
translations.idiomatic: With what breath remains I wish to fulfill my plain intent, hoping to lodge boundless longing and slightly extend unending feeling.

sentences.zh: 雖禮無明據，乃事有先例，率迷而至，必欲行之。

translations.literal: Though ritual has no clear warrant, yet the affair has earlier precedents; confused I arrive, yet I must do it.
translations.idiomatic: Though ritual has no clear warrant, the affair has precedents; confused I arrive, yet I must do it.

sentences.zh: 臨紙哽咽，言不識次。

translations.literal: Facing the paper I choke with sobs; words know no order.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the paper I choke with sobs; words know no order.

sentences.zh: 後為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令王晏弟詡為廣州，多納賕貨，昂依事劾奏，不憚權家，當時號為正直。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Xu Mian's younger brother Xu, in Guangzhou, took many bribes; Ang impeached according to the facts and did not fear the powerful house—contemporaries then called him upright.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian's brother Xu in Guangzhou took many bribes; Ang impeached on the facts without fearing the powerful—men then called him upright.

sentences.zh: 初，昂為洗馬，明帝為領軍，欽昂風素，頻降駕焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ang was Preceptor, Emperor Ming as Commander of the Palace Guard admired Ang's pure style and repeatedly descended to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang was Preceptor, Emperor Ming as Commander of the Palace Guard admired his pure style and repeatedly visited him.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，奏事多留與語，謂曰：「我昔以卿有美名，親經相詣。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he often kept Ang to talk when memorials were submitted and said, "I in old days because you had a fine name personally came to visit you."
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne he often kept Ang to talk after memorials and said, "In old days, because you had a fine name, I came to visit you myself."

sentences.zh: 」昂答曰：「陛下在田之日，遂蒙三顧草廬。

translations.literal: Ang answered, "When Your Majesty was in the fields, I indeed received three visits to the thatched hut."
translations.idiomatic: Ang answered, "When Your Majesty was in the fields, I indeed received three visits to the thatched hut."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋出為豫章內史，丁所生母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang and left office for mourning his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted Internal Administrator of Yuzhang and left office to mourn his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 以喪還，江路風潮暴駭，昂乃縛衣著柩，誓同沈溺。

translations.literal: Returning with the coffin, wind and waves on the river route raged violently; Ang then bound his garments and put on the coffin, vowing to sink together.
translations.idiomatic: Returning with the coffin, river wind and waves raged; Ang bound his garments to the coffin, vowing to sink together.

sentences.zh: 及風止，餘船皆沒，唯昂船獲全，咸謂精誠所致。

translations.literal: When the wind stopped, all other boats were lost; only Ang's boat was preserved whole—men all said it came from sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When the wind stopped, every other boat was lost; only Ang's was whole—men said it came from sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 葬訖，起為吳興太守。

translations.literal: After burial he was raised up as Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he was raised Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永元末，梁武帝起兵，州郡望風皆降，昂獨拒境。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops; commanderies and provinces bowed to the wind and all surrendered—only Ang closed his borders and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongyuan, Liang's Emperor Wu raised troops; provinces bowed to the wind and surrendered—only Ang closed his borders and resisted.

sentences.zh: 帝手書喻之曰：

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in his own hand to instruct him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand to instruct him:

sentences.zh: 夫禍福無門，興亡有數，天之所棄，人孰能匡。

translations.literal: Fortune and disaster have no gate; rise and fall have their number; what Heaven abandons, who can set aright?
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and disaster have no gate; rise and fall have their number; what Heaven abandons, who can set aright?

sentences.zh: 機來不再，圖之宜早。

translations.literal: The moment does not come twice; to plan, the time should be early.
translations.idiomatic: The moment does not come twice; to plan, the time should be early.

sentences.zh: 頃藉聽道路，承欲狼顧一隅，既未喻雅懷，聊申往意。

translations.literal: Recently, listening on the road, I heard you mean to look back at one corner; not yet understanding your refined intent, I briefly state my former meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, listening on the road, I heard you mean to hold one corner; not yet understanding your refined intent, I briefly state my former meaning.

sentences.zh: 獨夫狂悖，振古未聞，窮凶極虐，歲月滋甚。

translations.literal: The lone tyrant is mad and perverse, unheard of since antiquity; extreme cruelty grows month by month.
translations.idiomatic: The lone tyrant is mad and perverse, unheard of since antiquity; extreme cruelty grows month by month.

sentences.zh: 天未絕齊，聖明啟運，億兆有賴，百姓來蘇。

translations.literal: Heaven has not yet ended Qi; the sage and bright opens the mandate; the hundred millions have reliance; the hundred surnames are reborn.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has not yet ended Qi; the sage and bright opens the mandate; millions have reliance; people are reborn.

sentences.zh: 吾荷任前驅，掃除京邑，屠潰之期，當不雲遠。

translations.literal: I bear the former charge as vanguard, sweeping clean the capital region; the day of slaughter and rout should not be far off in clouds.
translations.idiomatic: I bear the former charge as vanguard, sweeping the capital; the day of slaughter and rout should not be far.

sentences.zh: 兼熒惑出端門，太白入氐室，天文表於上，人事符於下，不謀同契，實在茲辰。

translations.literal: Moreover Yinghuo exits the Gate of Integrity and Great White enters the Chamber of Foundation—heaven's signs appear above and human affairs match below; not to plan together—the time is truly this day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Mars exits the Gate of Integrity and Venus enters the Chamber of Foundation—heaven's signs appear above and human affairs match below; not to plan together—the time is truly this day.

sentences.zh: 且范岫、申胄久薦誠款，各率所守，仍為掎角；

translations.literal: Moreover Fan Xiu and Shen Zhou long offered sincere loyalty, each holding his command and still forming pincers;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Fan Xiu and Shen Zhou long offered sincere loyalty, each holding command and forming pincers;

sentences.zh: 而足下欲以區區之郡，禦堂堂之師，根本既傾，枝葉安附？

translations.literal: yet you wish with a tiny commandery to oppose a grand army—once the root is overturned, how can branches and leaves depend?
translations.idiomatic: yet you wish with a tiny commandery to oppose a grand army—once the root is overturned, how can branches depend?

sentences.zh: 今竭力昏主，未足為忠，家門屠滅，非所謂孝。

translations.literal: Now to exhaust strength for a dark lord is not enough for loyalty; to have one's household slaughtered and extinguished is not what is called filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust strength for a dark lord is not loyalty; to have one's house slaughtered is not filial piety.

sentences.zh: 忠孝俱盡，將欲何依，去就之宜，幸加詳擇。

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety both exhausted—on what will you rely? On going or staying, may you add careful choice.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety both exhausted—on what will you rely? On going or staying, choose carefully.

sentences.zh: 昂答曰：

translations.literal: Ang replied:
translations.idiomatic: Ang replied:

sentences.zh: 都史至辱誨，承藉以眾論，謂僕有勤王之舉，兼蒙誚責，獨無送款。

translations.literal: When the commandery clerk arrived I was shamed by your letter; relying on the crowd's talk, they say I had the deed of aiding the king, yet I alone was reproached for not sending allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery clerk arrived I was shamed by your letter; relying on crowd talk, they say I had the deed of aiding the king, yet I alone was reproached for not sending allegiance.

sentences.zh: 循復嚴旨，若臨萬仞。

translations.literal: Turning again to your stern command, it is like facing ten thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Turning again to your stern command is like facing ten thousand ren.

sentences.zh: 三吳內地，非用兵之所，況以偏隅一郡，何能為役？

translations.literal: The Three Wu interior is no place for using troops; how much the less can one corner of a remote commandery serve as a tool?
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu interior is no place for troops; how much less can one remote corner serve as a tool?

sentences.zh: 近奉敕，以此境多虞，見使安慰。

translations.literal: Recently I received an edict that because this territory has many troubles I was sent to reassure it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I received an edict that because this territory has many troubles I was sent to reassure it.

sentences.zh: 自承麾旆屆止，莫不膝袒軍門，唯僕一人敢後至者，正以自揆庸素，文武無施，直是陳國賤男子耳。

translations.literal: Since your banners and flags arrived and halted, none failed to bare knee and breast at the army gate—only I alone dared come last, precisely because measuring my plain mediocrity, in civil and military I have no accomplishment, I am simply a lowly man of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Since your banners arrived, none failed to bare knee and breast at the army gate—only I dared come last, precisely because I am a plain, unaccomplished man of Chen.

sentences.zh: 雖欲獻心，不增大軍之勇，置其愚默，甯沮眾帥之威。

translations.literal: Though I wish to offer my heart, I do not increase the great army's courage; leave me in silence and stupidity, and better not damp the commanders' prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Though I wish to offer loyalty, I add nothing to the army's courage; leave me in silence and I will not damp the commanders' prestige.

sentences.zh: 幸藉將軍含弘之大，可得從容以禮。

translations.literal: I venture to rely on the general's great forbearance, that I may be treated with ritual at ease.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to rely on the general's forbearance, that I may be treated with ritual at ease.

sentences.zh: 竊以一飧微施，尚復投殞；

translations.literal: I hold that one meal's tiny favor still brings one to cast away life;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that one meal's tiny favor still brings one to cast away life;

sentences.zh: 況食人之祿，而頓忘一旦，非唯物議不可，亦恐明公鄙之。

translations.literal: how much the more when eating another's salary suddenly to forget it in a morning—not only would public opinion not allow it, I also fear the enlightened lord would despise it.
translations.idiomatic: how much more when eating another's salary to forget it overnight—not only would public opinion forbid it, I fear the enlightened lord would despise it.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，昂舉哀慟哭。

translations.literal: When Jiankang fell, Ang raised mourning and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Ang raised mourning and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 時帝使豫州刺史李元履巡撫東土，敕元履曰：「袁昂道素之門，世有忠節，天下須共容之，勿以兵威陵辱。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor sent Inspector of Yuzhou Li Yuanyu to pacify the eastern lands and instructed Yuanyu, saying, "The Yuan clan's way and lineage is a house of loyalty through the generations; the realm must together tolerate them—do not use military might to insult them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuzhou Inspector Li Yuanyu to pacify the east and instructed him: "The Yuan house is loyalty through generations; the realm must tolerate them—do not insult them with military might."

sentences.zh: 」元履至宣旨，昂亦不請降，開門徹備而已。

translations.literal: Yuanyu arrived and announced the intent; Ang also did not ask to surrender, only opening the gates and removing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu arrived and announced the intent; Ang did not ask to surrender, only opening the gates and removing defenses.

sentences.zh: 及至，帝亦不問其過。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor also did not question his fault.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor also did not question his fault.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，以為後軍臨川王參軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was made staff officer to Prince of Linchuan, Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 2 he was made staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan, Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 昂啟謝曰：

translations.literal: Ang opened a memorial of thanks, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ang opened a memorial of thanks:

sentences.zh: 恩隆絕望之辰，慶集冥心之日，焰灰非喻，荑枯未擬。

translations.literal: Favor lofty in the season of cut-off hope; fortune gathered on the day of darkened heart—flame ash is no likeness, tender sprout on withered root no comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Favor lofty in the season of cut-off hope; fortune gathered on the day of darkened heart—flame ash is no likeness, tender sprout on withered root no comparison.

sentences.zh: 摳衣聚足，顛狽不勝。

translations.literal: Gathering robe and gathering foot, I am overwhelmed beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering robe and foot, I am overwhelmed beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 臣遍曆三墳，備詳六典，巡校賞罰之科，洞檢生死之律，莫不嚴五辟於明君之朝，峻三章於聖主之日。

translations.literal: Your servant has gone through the Three Canon, fully detailed the Six Classics, examined the standards of reward and punishment, thoroughly inspected the laws of life and death—none fail to make strict the five punishments in the enlightened ruler's court and steep the three chapters in the sage lord's day.
translations.idiomatic: I have gone through the Three Canon, fully detailed the Six Classics, examined reward and punishment, inspected life and death—none fail to make strict the five punishments in the enlightened court and steep the three chapters in the sage lord's day.

sentences.zh: 是以塗山始會，致防風之誅，酆邑方構，有崇侯之伐。

translations.literal: Therefore at Tushan's first assembly came the execution of Fangfeng; when Fengyi was just built came the attack on Chong Hou.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at Tushan's first assembly came Fangfeng's execution; when Fengyi was built came the attack on Chong Hou.

sentences.zh: 未有緩憲於斮戮之人，賒刑於耐罪之族，出萬死入一生如臣者也。

translations.literal: Never was lenient law applied to men of beheading and slaughter, nor deferred punishment to clans of lesser guilt—to go from ten thousand deaths into one life like your servant has not occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Never was lenient law applied to men marked for beheading, nor deferred punishment to clans of lesser guilt—to go from ten thousand deaths into one life like me has not occurred.

sentences.zh: 推恩及罪，在臣實大，披心瀝血，敢乞言之。

translations.literal: Extending grace even to guilt—in your servant it is truly great; baring heart and dripping blood, I dare beg to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Extending grace even to guilt—in me it is truly great; baring heart and dripping blood, I dare speak.

sentences.zh: 臣東國賤人，學行何取，既殊鳴雁直木，固無結綬彈冠，徒藉羽儀，易農就仕。

translations.literal: Your servant, a lowly man of the eastern state—what learning or conduct do I possess? Unlike the calling goose and straight tree, I truly had no tying of seal or plucking of cap; I merely borrowed insignia to change from farming and take office.
translations.idiomatic: I am a lowly man of the eastern state—what learning or conduct do I possess? Unlike the calling goose and straight tree, I had no tying of seal or plucking of cap; I merely borrowed insignia to leave farming for office.

sentences.zh: 往年濫職，守秩東隅，仰屬龔行，風驅電掩，當其時也，負鼎圖者日至，執玉帛者相望；

translations.literal: In former years I wrongly held office, keeping rank in the eastern corner; looking up I belonged to the campaign of righteous march, wind-driven and lightning-swift; at that time those bearing cauldrons came daily, those holding jade and silk were seen one after another;
translations.idiomatic: In former years I wrongly held office in the east; looking up I belonged to the righteous march, wind-driven and lightning-swift; then those bearing cauldrons came daily, those holding jade and silk were seen one after another;

sentences.zh: 獨在愚臣，頓昏大義，徇鴻毛之輕，忘同德之重。

translations.literal: only I, the foolish minister, suddenly dim to the great principle, followed the lightness of a goose feather and forgot the weight of shared virtue.
translations.idiomatic: only I, the foolish minister, suddenly dim to the great principle, followed the lightness of a goose feather and forgot the weight of shared virtue.

sentences.zh: 但三吳險薄，五湖交通，屢起田儋之變，每懼殷通之禍，空慕君魚保境，遂失師涓抱器。

translations.literal: But the Three Wu are dangerous and thin, the Five Lakes connect in traffic; Tian Dan's changes often rose, and I always feared Yin Tong's disaster; vainly I admired Lord Jun's fish preserving the territory, and so lost Master Juan's embrace of the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: But the Three Wu are dangerous, the Five Lakes connect; Tian Dan's changes often rose, and I feared Yin Tong's disaster; vainly I admired preserving the territory like Lord Jun, and lost Master Juan's embrace of the vessel.

sentences.zh: 後至者斬，臣甘斯戮，明刑徇眾，誰曰不然。

translations.literal: Those who come late are beheaded—I willingly accept that punishment; bright punishment for the crowd—who says otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: Those who come late are beheaded—I willingly accept that punishment; bright punishment for the crowd—who says otherwise?

sentences.zh: 幸因約法之弘，承解網之宥，猶當降等薪粲，遂乃頓釋鉗赭。

translations.literal: Fortunately through the mercy of contracted law and the pardon of loosened net, I should still have been lowered like Xin and Cai, yet suddenly the shackles and red were cast off.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately through the mercy of contracted law and the pardon of loosened net, I should still have been lowered like Xin and Cai, yet suddenly shackles and red were cast off.

sentences.zh: 斂骨吹魂，還編黔庶，濯疵蕩穢，入楚游陳，天波既洗，雲油遽沐。

translations.literal: Gathering bones and blowing soul, returned to rank among the black-headed; washing stain and scouring filth, entering Chu and wandering Chen—Heaven's wave has washed, cloud oil has suddenly bathed.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering bones and blowing soul, returned to rank among commoners; washing stain and scouring filth, entering Chu and wandering Chen—Heaven's wave has washed, cloud oil has bathed.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：非死之難，處死之難。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: not that dying is hard, but that facing death is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: not that dying is hard, but that facing death is hard.

sentences.zh: 臣之所荷，曠古不書，臣之所死，未知何地。

translations.literal: What your servant bears is unwritten since remotest antiquity; where your servant dies, I do not yet know what place.
translations.idiomatic: What I bear is unwritten since remotest antiquity; where I die, I do not yet know.

sentences.zh: 武帝答曰：「朕遺射鉤，卿無自外。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu replied, "I leave aside the matter of the bowstring hook—you need not put yourself outside."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replied, "I leave aside the bowstring hook—you need not put yourself outside."

sentences.zh: 尋為侍中，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he became Palace Attendant and was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「齊明帝用卿為黑頭尚書，我用卿為白頭尚書，良以多愧。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "Emperor Ming of Qi used you as a dark-haired Director of Personnel; I use you as a white-haired Director of Personnel—I am truly much ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Qi Mingdi used you as a dark-haired Director of Personnel; I use you as a white-haired Director of Personnel—I am truly ashamed."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣生四十七年於茲矣，四十以前，臣之自有，七年以後，陛下所養。

translations.literal: He answered, "Your servant has lived forty-seven years to now; forty years before were mine by right, seven years after are what Your Majesty nourished."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have lived forty-seven years; forty before were mine by right, seven after are what Your Majesty nourished."

sentences.zh: 七歲尚書，未為晚達。

translations.literal: Director of Personnel at seven years is not late attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Personnel at seven years is not late attainment.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「士固不妄有名。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "A gentleman truly does not vainly have a name."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A gentleman truly does not vainly have a name."

sentences.zh: 十五年，為尚書左僕射，尋為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon Director.

sentences.zh: 時僕射徐勉勢傾天下，在昂處宴，賓主甚歡。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Xu Mian's power tilted the realm; at Ang's place they feasted, host and guest very merry.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian's power tilted the realm; at Ang's house they feasted, host and guest very merry.

sentences.zh: 勉求昂出內人傳杯，昂良久不出，勉苦求之。

translations.literal: Mian asked Ang to send out inner-chamber women to pass cups; Ang for a long while would not come out; Mian bitterly pressed the request.
translations.idiomatic: Mian asked Ang to send inner-chamber women to pass cups; Ang long would not come out; Mian pressed hard.

sentences.zh: 昂不獲已，命出五六人，始至齋合，昂謂勉曰：「我無少年，老嫗並是兒母，非王妃母，便是主大家，今令問訊卿。

translations.literal: Ang could not avoid it and ordered five or six women out; when they reached the study gate Ang said to Mian, "I have no young women—all the old matrons are sons' mothers, not the princess consort's mother or the chief lady of the house; now I have them greet you."
translations.idiomatic: Ang could not avoid it and ordered five or six women out; at the study gate he told Mian, "I have no young women—all the old matrons are sons' mothers, not the princess consort's mother or the chief lady; now I have them greet you."

sentences.zh: 」勉聞大驚求止，方知昂為貴。

translations.literal: Mian, hearing, was greatly alarmed and begged to stop; only then did he know Ang's nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, hearing, was alarmed and begged to stop; only then did he know Ang's nobility.

sentences.zh: 昂雅有人鑒，遊處不雜，入其門者號登龍門。

translations.literal: Ang elegantly had discernment of men; in going and staying he did not mix; those entering his gate were called climbing the Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had elegant discernment of men; in company he did not mix; those entering his gate were said to climb the Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 大通中，位司空，大同六年，薨，時年八十。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he reached Minister of Works; in the sixth year of Datong he died, then aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong he reached Minister of Works; in Datong 6 he died, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 詔即日舉哀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered mourning raised that same day.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered mourning raised that same day.

sentences.zh: 初，昂臨終遺疏不受贈諡，敕諸子不得言上行狀及立銘志，凡有所須，悉皆停省。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ang was near death his final memorial would not accept posthumous enfeoffment or posthumous title; he charged his sons not to speak of the late ruler's conduct or set up inscription and record; whatever was needed, all was to be stopped and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Near death his final memorial refused posthumous enfeoffment or title; he charged his sons not to praise the late ruler's conduct or set up inscription; whatever was needed, all was to be stopped.

sentences.zh: 因復曰：「吾釋褐從仕，不期富貴，但官序不失等倫，衣食粗知榮辱，以此闔棺，無慚鄉里。

translations.literal: He also said, "I from first taking office did not expect wealth and honor, but only that rank and order not lose their sequence and clothing and food roughly know honor and shame—with this to close the coffin I am not ashamed before the village."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "From first office I expected no wealth, only that rank keep its order and clothing and food roughly know honor and shame—with this to close the coffin I am not ashamed before the village."

sentences.zh: 往忝吳興，屬在昏明之際，既闇於前覺，無誠於聖朝，不識天命，甘貽顯戮，幸遇殊恩，得全門戶。

translations.literal: Formerly I wrongly served Wu Commandery, belonging to the time between dark and bright; already dim to foreknowledge, without sincerity toward the holy court, not knowing Heaven's mandate, willingly bringing bright execution—fortunately meeting special grace, able to preserve the gate and household.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly I wrongly served Wu Commandery in the time between dark and bright; dim to foreknowledge, without sincerity toward the holy court, not knowing Heaven's mandate, willingly bringing execution—fortunately meeting special grace, preserving the gate and household.

sentences.zh: 自念負罪私門，階榮望絕，保存性命，以為幸甚，不謂叨竊寵靈，一至於此。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I bore guilt in my private gate and steps to glory were cut off, preserving life I thought greatly fortunate—I never thought to steal favor and numinous blessing to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that I bore guilt in my private gate and steps to glory were cut off, preserving life I thought greatly fortunate—I never thought to steal favor to this degree.

sentences.zh: 常欲竭誠酬報，申吾乃心，所以朝廷每興師北伐，吾輒啟求行。

translations.literal: I always wished to exhaust sincerity in repayment and declare my heart; therefore whenever the court raised troops for northern campaign I always opened a memorial asking to go.
translations.idiomatic: I always wished to repay with exhausted sincerity; therefore whenever the court raised northern troops I always memorialized asking to go.

sentences.zh: 誓之丹款，實非矯言。

translations.literal: The oath in cinnabar sincerity was truly not pretended words.
translations.idiomatic: The oath in cinnabar sincerity was truly not pretended words.

sentences.zh: 既庸懦無施，皆不蒙許，雖欲罄命，其議莫從。

translations.literal: Since I was cowardly and weak without accomplishment, none was permitted; though I wished to exhaust life, the deliberation would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Since I was cowardly and weak without accomplishment, none was permitted; though I wished to exhaust life, deliberation would not follow.

sentences.zh: 今日瞑目，畢恨泉壤，聖朝遵古，如吾名品，或有追遠之恩，脫有贈官，慎勿祗奉。

translations.literal: Today closing eyes, full regret in the spring mound; the holy court follows antiquity—like my name and rank there may be grace of distant pursuit; if there is posthumous office, carefully do not receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Today closing eyes, full regret in the grave; the holy court follows antiquity—for a man of my name and rank there may be grace of distant pursuit; if there is posthumous office, carefully do not receive it.

sentences.zh: 」諸子累表陳奏，詔不許，諡曰穆正公。

translations.literal: The sons repeatedly memorialized; an edict would not permit it; posthumous title Duke of Reverent Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The sons repeatedly memorialized; an edict would not permit refusal; posthumous title Duke of Reverent Integrity.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: There is a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，昂之歸梁，有馬仙琕者亦以義烈稱。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ang returned to Liang, there was also Ma Xianbi, famed likewise for righteous fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang returned to Liang, Ma Xianbi was also famed for righteous fierceness.

sentences.zh: 附 馬仙琕

translations.literal: Appendix: Ma Xianbi
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Ma Xianbi

sentences.zh: 仙琕字靈馥，扶風郿人。

translations.literal: Xianbi, styled Lingfu, was a man of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi, courtesy name Lingfu, was a man of Mei in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父伯鸞，宋冠軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Boluan served Song as Marshal of the Champion Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Boluan served Song as Marshal of the Champion Army.

sentences.zh: 仙琕少以果敢聞，父憂毀瘠過禮，負土成墳，手植松柏。

translations.literal: Xianbi from youth was known for bold decisiveness; when his father died his grief wasted him beyond ritual; he himself carried earth to form the mound and with his hands planted pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi from youth was known for bold decisiveness; when his father died his grief wasted him beyond ritual; he carried earth for the mound and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 仕齊位豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he reached Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he reached Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁武起兵，使其故人姚仲賓說之，仙琕先為設酒，乃斬於軍門以徇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops he sent his old acquaintance Yao Zhongbin to persuade him; Xianbi first set out wine for him, then beheaded him at the army gate as warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu raised troops he sent old acquaintance Yao Zhongbin to persuade him; Xianbi first set out wine, then beheaded him at the army gate as warning.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣其族叔懷遠說之，仙琕曰：「大義滅親。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent his clansman uncle Huaiyuan to persuade him; Xianbi said, "Great righteousness destroys kin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent clansman uncle Huaiyuan to persuade him; Xianbi said, "Great righteousness destroys kin."

sentences.zh: 」又命斬之。

translations.literal: He again ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He again ordered him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 懷遠號泣，軍中為請乃免。

translations.literal: Huaiyuan wailed; the army interceded for him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyuan wailed; the army interceded and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 武帝至新林，仙琕猶於江西日抄運漕。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Xinlin, Xianbi still on the west of the river daily raided transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Xinlin, Xianbi still west of the river daily raided transport grain.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，仙琕舉哀謂眾曰：「我受人任寄，義不容降，今眾寡不侔，勢必屠滅。

translations.literal: When Jiankang fell, Xianbi raised mourning and told the crowd, "I received men's trust and charge; righteousness does not permit surrender—now our numbers do not match and we shall surely be slaughtered and destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Xianbi raised mourning and told the crowd, "I received men's trust; righteousness forbids surrender—our numbers do not match and we shall be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 公等雖無二心，其如親老何。

translations.literal: You though without two hearts—what of your aged parents?
translations.idiomatic: You though without divided hearts—what of your aged parents?

sentences.zh: 我為忠臣，君為孝子，各盡其道，不亦可乎。

translations.literal: I will be the loyal minister, you the filial sons—each fulfilling his path—is that not also fitting?
translations.idiomatic: I will be the loyal minister, you the filial sons—each fulfilling his path—is that not fitting?

sentences.zh: 」於是悉遣城內兵出降，余壯士數十，閉門獨守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent all soldiers within the city out to surrender; several dozen stalwart men remained, closed the gate, and alone held defense.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent all soldiers within the city out to surrender; several dozen stalwart men remained, closed the gate, and alone held defense.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵入，圍之數十重。

translations.literal: Presently troops entered and surrounded them in several tens of rings.
translations.idiomatic: Presently troops entered and surrounded them in tens of rings.

sentences.zh: 仙琕令士皆持滿，兵不敢近。

translations.literal: Xianbi ordered the men all to hold bows drawn full; the soldiers did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi ordered the men all to hold bows fully drawn; the soldiers did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 日晚乃投弓曰：「諸君但來見取，我義不降。

translations.literal: When the day grew late he cast down his bow and said, "You all come take me—I by righteousness will not surrender."
translations.idiomatic: When day grew late he cast down his bow and said, "Come take me—I by righteousness will not surrender."

sentences.zh: 」乃檻送建康，至石頭而脫之。

translations.literal: He was then caged and sent to Jiankang; reaching Shitou he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was caged and sent to Jiankang; reaching Shitou he was released.

sentences.zh: 帝使待袁昂至俱入，曰：「使天下見二義士。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that he wait until Yuan Ang arrived and enter together, saying, "Let the realm see two men of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to wait until Yuan Ang arrived and enter together: "Let the realm see two men of righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」帝勞之曰：「射鉤斬驅，昔人弗忌，卿勿以戮使斷運苟自嫌絕也。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying, "Shooting the hook and beheading the driver—in old days men did not resent it; do not because of cutting transport vainly suspect and cut yourself off."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him: "Shooting the hook and beheading the driver—in old days men did not resent it; do not because of cutting transport vainly suspect and cut yourself off."

sentences.zh: 」謝曰：「小人如失主犬，後主飼之，便復為用。

translations.literal: He thanked him, saying, "A petty man is like a dog who lost his master; when the later master feeds him, he again serves."
translations.idiomatic: He thanked him: "A petty man is like a dog who lost his master; when the later master feeds him, he serves again."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑而美之。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and praised him.

sentences.zh: 俄而母卒，帝知其貧，賻給甚厚。

translations.literal: Presently his mother died; the emperor knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Presently his mother died; the emperor knew he was poor and gave funeral gifts very generously.

sentences.zh: 仙琕號泣謂弟仲艾曰：「蒙大造之恩，未獲上報，今復荷殊澤，當與爾以心力自效耳。」

translations.literal: Xianbi wailed and told his younger brother Zhong'ai, "I received great creating grace and have not yet repaid it; now again I receive special favor—I shall with you exert heart and strength to serve."
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi wailed and told younger brother Zhong'ai, "I received great creating grace and have not repaid it; now again special favor—I shall with you exert heart and strength to serve."

sentences.zh: 天監四年，師侵魏，仙琕每戰，恒冠三軍，與諸將論議，口未嘗言功。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian the army invaded Wei; Xianbi in every battle always led the three armies; with the generals in discussion he never spoke of merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 4 the army invaded Wei; Xianbi in every battle always led the three armies; with generals in discussion he never spoke of merit.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，仙琕曰：「大丈夫為時所知，當進不求名，退不逃罪，乃平生願也，何功可論？

translations.literal: When men asked the reason, Xianbi said, "A great husband, when known by the age, should advance without seeking name and retreat without fleeing guilt—that is the wish of a lifetime; what merit is there to discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: When men asked why, Xianbi said, "A great man known by the age should advance without seeking name and retreat without fleeing guilt—that is life's wish; what merit is there to discuss?"

sentences.zh: 」為南義陽太守，累破山蠻，郡境清謐。

translations.literal: He was Administrator of Southern Yiyang, repeatedly broke the mountain barbarians, and the commandery borders were quiet and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was Administrator of Southern Yiyang, repeatedly broke the mountain barbarians, and the commandery was quiet.

sentences.zh: 以功封浛洭縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Hanji.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Earl of Hanji.

sentences.zh: 遷司州刺史，進號貞威將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Sizhou and promoted in title to General of Upright Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred Inspector of Sizhou and promoted General of Upright Might.

sentences.zh: 魏豫州人白早生使以懸瓠來降，武帝使仙琕赴之，又遣直合將軍武會超、馬廣率眾為援。

translations.literal: Bai Zaosheng of Wei Yuzhou sent word offering Xuanshi in surrender; Emperor Wu sent Xianbi to go and also sent the Direct Attendant General Wu Huichao and Ma Guang leading troops as support.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zaosheng of Wei Yuzhou offered Xuanshi in surrender; Emperor Wu sent Xianbi and Direct Attendant General Wu Huichao and Ma Guang as support.

sentences.zh: 仙琕進頓楚王城，遣副將齊苟兒助守懸瓠。

translations.literal: Xianbi advanced and encamped at Prince of Chu's city, sending Deputy General Qi Gou'er to help defend Xuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi advanced to Prince of Chu's city, sending Deputy General Qi Gou'er to help defend Xuanshi.

sentences.zh: 魏中山王英攻懸瓠，執齊苟兒，進禽馬廣送洛陽，仙琕不能救。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Ying attacked Xuanshi, captured Qi Gou'er, advanced and captured Ma Guang sending him to Luoyang; Xianbi could not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Zhongshan attacked Xuanshi, captured Qi Gou'er, captured Ma Guang and sent him to Luoyang; Xianbi could not save them.

sentences.zh: 會超等亦相次退散，魏軍進據三關，仙琕坐征還為雲騎將軍。

translations.literal: Huichao and the others also successively withdrew and scattered; Wei armies advanced and occupied the Three Passes; Xianbi was dismissed and returned as General of Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Huichao and others withdrew; Wei armies occupied the Three Passes; Xianbi was dismissed and returned General of Cloud Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十年，朐山人殺琅邪太守劉晰，以城降魏，詔假仙琕節討之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the people of Xiongshan killed Administrator of Langye Liu Xi and surrendered the city to Wei; an edict lent Xianbi credentials to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Xiongshan people killed Langye Administrator Liu Xi and surrendered to Wei; an edict lent Xianbi credentials to attack.

sentences.zh: 魏徐州刺史盧昶以眾十餘萬赴焉，仙琕累戰破走之。

translations.literal: Wei Inspector of Xuzhou Lu Chang came with more than a hundred thousand men; Xianbi repeatedly fought, broke them, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuzhou Inspector Lu Chang came with more than a hundred thousand; Xianbi repeatedly fought, broke them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，遷豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted in rank to marquis, transferred to Inspector of Yuzhou, and additionally made Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted marquis, transferred Inspector of Yuzhou, and made Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 仙琕自為將及居州郡，能與士卒同勞逸，身衣不過布帛，所居無幃幕衾屏，行則飲食與塚養最下者同。

translations.literal: From the time he was general and in commandery and province he could share toil and rest with officers and soldiers; his body clothes were no more than cloth and silk; where he dwelt there were no curtains, quilts, or screens; on march his food and drink were the same as the lowest camp followers.
translations.idiomatic: From general to commandery and province he shared toil and rest with officers and soldiers; his clothes were cloth and silk; his dwelling had no curtains or screens; on march he ate and drank like the lowest camp followers.

sentences.zh: 其在邊境，常單身潛入敵境，伺知壁壘村落險要處所，攻戰多克捷，士卒亦甘心為用，帝雅愛仗之。

translations.literal: On the borders he often alone secretly entered enemy territory, reconnoitering walls, villages, and places of strategic importance; in attack and battle he often achieved victory, and officers and soldiers also willingly served him; the emperor greatly loved and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: On the borders he often alone secretly entered enemy territory, reconnoitering walls and villages; in battle he often won, and soldiers willingly served him; the emperor greatly loved and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 卒于州，贈左衛將軍，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumously made General of the Left Guard; posthumous title Gang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the province; posthumously made General of the Left Guard; posthumous title Gang.

sentences.zh: 初，仙琕幼名仙婢，及長以婢名不典，乃以玉代女云。

translations.literal: Earlier Xianbi's childhood name was Xianbi; when grown, because the name with 'bi' was not elegant, he replaced the woman radical with jade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xianbi's childhood name used the 'woman' radical; when grown, because it was inelegant, he replaced it with jade.

sentences.zh: 子岩夫嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yanfu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanfu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 昂子 君正

translations.literal: Ang's son Junzheng
translations.idiomatic: Ang's son Junzheng

sentences.zh: 昂子君正字世忠，少聰敏。

translations.literal: Junzheng, styled Shizhong, was clever from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng, courtesy name Shizhong, was clever from youth.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，父疾，晝夜不眠，專侍左右。

translations.literal: When he was a few years old his father was ill; day and night he did not sleep, attending solely at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When he was a few years old his father was ill; day and night he did not sleep, attending solely at his side.

sentences.zh: 家人勸令暫臥，答曰：「官既未差，眠亦不安。

translations.literal: The household urged him to rest briefly; he answered, "Since the official is not yet recovered, sleep is also not at ease."
translations.idiomatic: The household urged rest; he answered, "Since father is not yet recovered, sleep is also not at ease."

sentences.zh: 」歷位太子庶子。

translations.literal: He held office as Supervisor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He held office as Supervisor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 君正美風儀，善自居處，以貴公子早得時譽。

translations.literal: Junzheng had fine bearing and was skilled at comportment; as a noble scion he early gained contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng had fine bearing and skilled comportment; as a noble scion he early gained reputation.

sentences.zh: 為豫章內史。

translations.literal: He was Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 性不信巫邪，有師萬世榮稱道術，為一郡巫長。

translations.literal: By nature he did not believe in shamans and heterodoxies; there was a master Wan Shirong who claimed the Way and was chief shaman of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he did not believe shamans or heterodoxies; Master Wan Shirong claimed the Way and was chief shaman of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 君正在郡小疾，主簿熊嶽薦之。

translations.literal: Junzheng in the commandery had a slight illness; Chief Clerk Xiong Yue recommended the master.
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng in the commandery had a slight illness; Chief Clerk Xiong Yue recommended the master.

sentences.zh: 師云：「須疾者衣為信命。

translations.literal: The master said, "The ill person's garment is needed as token of fate."
translations.idiomatic: The master said, "The ill person's garment is needed as token of fate."

sentences.zh: 」君正以所著襦與之，事竟取襦，云：「神將送與北斗君」。

translations.literal: Junzheng gave the jacket he was wearing; when the affair ended the master took the jacket, saying, "The spirit will send it to the Lord of the Northern Dipper."
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng gave the jacket he wore; when the affair ended the master took it, saying, "The spirit will send it to the Lord of the Northern Dipper."

sentences.zh: 君正使檢諸身，於衣裏獲之，以為亂政，即刑於市而焚神，一郡無敢行巫。

translations.literal: Junzheng had his person search his body and recovered it from inside the garment; thinking it disorder of government, he at once executed him in the market and burned the spirit-image; the whole commandery dared not practice shamanism.
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng had his person search and recovered it from inside the garment; thinking it disorder of government, he executed the master in the market and burned the spirit-image; the whole commandery dared not practice shamanism.

sentences.zh: 遷吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，率數百人隨邵陵王綸赴援，及台城陷，還郡。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled he led several hundred men following Prince of Shaoling Lun to go to aid; when the capital fell he returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled he led several hundred men following Prince Lun of Shaoling to aid; when the capital fell he returned to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 君正當官蒞事有名稱，而蓄聚財產，服玩靡麗。

translations.literal: Junzheng in holding office and attending to affairs had a name for competence, yet he amassed property and his dress and playthings were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng in office had a name for competence, yet he amassed property and his dress and playthings were lavish.

sentences.zh: 賊遣張太墨攻之，新城戍主戴僧易勸令拒守，己以戍兵自外擊之，君正不能決。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Zhang Taimo to attack; New City garrison commander Dai Sengyi urged him to hold defense, himself taking garrison troops to strike from outside; Junzheng could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels sent Zhang Taimo to attack; New City garrison commander Dai Sengyi urged defense, himself striking from outside with garrison troops; Junzheng could not decide.

sentences.zh: 吳人陸映公等懼不濟，賊種族其家，勸之迎賊。

translations.literal: Wu men Lu Yinggong and others feared failure and that the rebels would exterminate their clans, and urged welcoming the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wu men Lu Yinggong and others feared failure and rebel extermination of their clans, and urged welcoming the rebels.

sentences.zh: 君正性怯懦，乃送米及牛酒郊迎賊，賊掠奪其財物子女，因是感疾卒。

translations.literal: Junzheng was by nature timid and weak; he therefore sent rice and oxen and wine to the suburbs to welcome the rebels; the rebels plundered his property, women, and children, and he therefore sickened and died.
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng was timid; he sent rice, oxen, and wine to the suburbs to welcome the rebels; they plundered his property, women, and children, and he sickened and died.

sentences.zh: 子樞。

translations.literal: Son Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shu.

sentences.zh: 君正子 樞

translations.literal: Junzheng's son Shu
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng's son Shu

sentences.zh: 樞字踐言，美容儀，性沈靜，好學，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Jianyan, had fine appearance, was by nature quiet and deep, loved learning, and never let a scroll leave his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Jianyan, had fine looks, quiet depth, loved learning, and never let a scroll leave his hand.

sentences.zh: 家本顯貴，貲產充積，而樞獨處率素，傍無交往，非公事未嘗出遊，榮利之懷淡如也。

translations.literal: The family was originally eminent and wealthy with abundant assets, yet Shu alone lived plainly and simply, with no companions nearby; unless on public business he never went out wandering—thought of glory and profit was thin indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The family was eminent and wealthy, yet Shu alone lived plainly, with no companions nearby; unless on public business he never went out—glory and profit meant little to him.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，樞往吳郡省父疾，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Shu went to Wu Commandery to visit his father's illness and entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Shu went to Wu Commandery to visit his father's illness and entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 時四方擾亂，人求苟免，樞居喪以至孝聞。

translations.literal: At that time the four directions were disturbed and men sought mere escape; Shu in mourning became known for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was disturbed and men sought mere escape; Shu in mourning became known for utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯平侯景，鎮建鄴，衣冠爭往造請，樞杜門靜居，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian pacified Hou Jing and garrisoned Jiankang; officials and gentry vied to visit and request audience; Shu closed his gate and dwelt quietly, not seeking fame or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian pacified Hou Jing and garrisoned Jiankang; officials vied to visit; Shu closed his gate and dwelt quietly, not seeking fame.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，歷吏部尚書、吳興郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Shaotai era he served successively as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai he served as Director of Personnel and Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 陳永定中，徵為侍中，掌選。

translations.literal: In the Yongding era of Chen he was summoned as Palace Attendant and directed selection.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen's Yongding era he was summoned Palace Attendant and directed selection.

sentences.zh: 遷都官尚書，掌選如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Punishments, directing selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred Director of Punishments, directing selection as before.

sentences.zh: 樞博學，明悉舊章。

translations.literal: Shu was broadly learned and clearly knew old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was broadly learned and clearly knew old regulations.

sentences.zh: 初，陳武帝長女永嗣公主，先適陳留太守錢蕆，生子岊，主及岊並卒于梁時。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wu of Chen's eldest daughter Princess Yongsi had first been married to Administrator of Chenliu Qian Yi and bore a son Jie; the princess and Jie both died in Liang times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen's eldest daughter Princess Yongsi had first married Chenliu Administrator Qian Yi and bore son Jie; princess and Jie both died in Liang times.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，唯主追封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate, only the princess was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the mandate, only the princess was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 至是將葬，尚書請議加蕆駙馬都尉，並贈岊官。

translations.literal: At this, about to bury her, the Masters of Writing requested deliberation on additionally making Yi Commandant-consort to the princess and posthumously granting Jie office.
translations.idiomatic: At burial the Masters of Writing requested deliberation on additionally making Yi commandant-consort to the princess and posthumously granting Jie office.

sentences.zh: 樞議曰：

translations.literal: Shu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized:

sentences.zh: 時議以為當。

translations.literal: Contemporary deliberation held it correct.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary deliberation held it correct.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，為吏部尚書，領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjia he became Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia 3 he became Director of Personnel and concurrently Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 以葬父拜表自解，詔令葬訖停宅視郡事，服闋還職。

translations.literal: Because of burying his father he submitted a memorial requesting release from office; an edict ordered that after burial he stop at home and oversee commandery affairs, and after mourning ended return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Burying his father he requested release; an edict ordered after burial he stop at home and oversee commandery affairs, and after mourning return.

sentences.zh: 時僕射到仲舉雖參掌選事，銓衡汲引，並出於樞，舉薦多會上旨。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Dao Zhongju though sharing in directing selection, the balance of promotion and recommendation all came from Shu, and recommendations mostly accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Dao Zhongju though sharing selection, promotion and recommendation all came from Shu, and recommendations mostly accorded with imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 謹慎周密，清白自居，文武職司，鮮有遊其門者。

translations.literal: Careful, thorough, and dwelling in purity—among civil and military officeholders few wandered at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Careful, thorough, dwelling in purity—among civil and military officeholders few wandered at his gate.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，遷尚書左僕射，卒，諡曰簡懿。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he died; posthumous title Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he died; posthumous title Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: There is a collected works in ten scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in ten scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 弟憲。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Xian.

sentences.zh: 樞弟 憲

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Xian
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Xian

sentences.zh: 憲字德章，幼聰敏好學，有雅量。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Dezhang, from youth was clever, loved learning, and had elegant breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, courtesy name Dezhang, from youth was clever, loved learning, and had elegant breadth.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝修建庠序，別開五館，其一館在憲宅西，憲常招引諸生與之談論，新義出人意表，同輩咸嗟服焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang built schools and separately opened five halls; one hall was west of Xian's residence; Xian often invited students to discuss with them, new meanings exceeding men's expectations, and peers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang built schools and opened five halls; one stood west of Xian's residence; Xian often invited students to discuss, new meanings exceeding expectation, and peers sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 大同八年，武帝撰孔子正言章句，詔下國學宣制旨義。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, Emperor Wu compiled Correct Meaning chapter-and-sentence commentary on Confucius; an edict sent it down to the National University to proclaim the imperial meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 8 Emperor Wu compiled Correct Meaning commentary on Confucius; an edict sent it to the National University to proclaim the imperial meaning.

sentences.zh: 憲時年十四，被召為正言生，祭酒到溉目送之，愛其神采。

translations.literal: Xian was then fourteen, summoned as a Correct Meaning student; Libationer Dao Gai saw him off with his eyes, loving his spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was fourteen, summoned Correct Meaning student; Libationer Dao Gai saw him off with his eyes, loving his spirit.

sentences.zh: 國子博士周弘正謂憲父君正曰：「賢子今茲欲策試不？

translations.literal: National University Erudite Zhou Hongzheng said to Xian's father Junzheng, "Your worthy son—does he wish to take the policy examination now?"
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhou Hongzheng said to Xian's father Junzheng, "Your worthy son—does he wish to take the policy examination now?"

sentences.zh: 」君正曰：「未敢令試。

translations.literal: Junzheng said, "I do not yet dare have him tested."
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng said, "I do not yet dare have him tested."

sentences.zh: 」居數日，君正遣門客岑文豪與憲候弘正。

translations.literal: After several days Junzheng sent a client, Cen Wenhao, with Xian to wait on Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Junzheng sent client Cen Wenhao with Xian to wait on Hongzheng.

sentences.zh: 會弘正將升講坐，弟子異集，乃延憲入室，授以麈尾，令憲豎義。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng was about to ascend the lecture seat and disciples gathered in difference, he extended Xian into the room, gave him a fly-whisk, and ordered Xian to set forth the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng was about to lecture and disciples gathered, he brought Xian into the room, gave him a fly-whisk, and ordered him to set forth the meaning.

sentences.zh: 時謝岐、何妥在坐，弘正謂曰：「二賢雖窮奧賾，得無憚此後生邪？

translations.literal: At that time Xie Qi and He Tuo were seated; Hongzheng said to them, "You two sages though plumb the hidden deep—will you not fear this younger generation?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qi and He Tuo were seated; Hongzheng said, "You two sages though plumb the hidden deep—will you not fear this younger generation?"

sentences.zh: 」何、謝乃遞起義端，深極理致，憲與往復數番，酬對閑敏。

translations.literal: He and Xie then in turn raised points of meaning, reaching the deepest principle; Xian went back and forth several rounds, answering with easy quickness.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xie raised points of meaning to deepest principle; Xian went back and forth several rounds, answering with easy quickness.

sentences.zh: 弘正謂妥曰：「恣卿所問，勿以童幼期之。

translations.literal: Hongzheng said to Tuo, "Ask as you wish—do not expect childishness from him."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng said to Tuo, "Ask as you wish—do not expect childishness from him."

sentences.zh: 」時觀者重遝，憲神色自若，辯論有餘，弘正亦起數難，終不能屈。

translations.literal: At that time observers pressed in layers; Xian's expression was as usual and debate had surplus; Hongzheng also raised several difficulties and in the end could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Observers pressed in layers; Xian's expression was as usual and debate had surplus; Hongzheng raised several difficulties and could not bend him.

sentences.zh: 因告文豪曰：「卿還諮袁吳郡，此郎已堪見代博士矣。

translations.literal: He then told Wenhao, "Go consult Administrator Yuan of Wu—this youth already can replace the erudite."
translations.idiomatic: He told Wenhao, "Go consult Administrator Yuan of Wu—this youth already can replace the erudite."

sentences.zh: 」時生徒對策，多行賄賂，文豪請具束修。

translations.literal: At that time students answering policy often practiced bribery; Wenhao asked to prepare the bundle of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Students answering policy often practiced bribery; Wenhao asked to prepare the bundle of silk.

sentences.zh: 君正曰：「我豈能用錢為兒買第邪？

translations.literal: Junzheng said, "How could I use money to buy rank for my son?"
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng said, "How could I use money to buy rank for my son?"

sentences.zh: 」學司銜之。

translations.literal: The academy officials resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The academy officials resented this.

sentences.zh: 及憲試，爭起劇難，憲隨問抗答，剖析如流。

translations.literal: When Xian was tested, they all rose with fierce difficulties; Xian answered as asked, analyzing like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was tested, examiners rose with fierce difficulties; Xian answered as asked, analyzing like flowing water.

sentences.zh: 到溉顧憲曰：「袁君正其有後矣。

translations.literal: Dao Gai looked at Xian and said, "Yuan Junzheng truly has posterity."
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gai looked at Xian and said, "Yuan Junzheng truly has posterity."

sentences.zh: 」及君正將之吳郡，溉祖道於征虜亭，謂君正曰：「昨策生，蕭敏孫、徐孝克非不解義，至於風神器局，去賢子遠矣。

translations.literal: When Junzheng was about to go to Wu Commandery, Gai saw him off at the Captive-Slayer Pavilion and said to Junzheng, "Yesterday's policy student—Xiao Minsun and Xu Xiaoke are not without understanding of meaning, but in spirit, bearing, and composure they are far from your worthy son."
translations.idiomatic: When Junzheng was about to go to Wu Commandery, Gai saw him off at the Captive-Slayer Pavilion and said, "Yesterday's policy student—Xiao Minsun and Xu Xiaoke understand meaning, but in spirit and composure they are far from your son."

sentences.zh: 」尋舉高第，以貴公子選尚南沙公主，即梁簡文帝女也。

translations.literal: Soon he was nominated with highest marks and, as a noble scion, was selected to marry Princess of Nansha—she was the daughter of Emperor Jian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was nominated with highest marks and, as noble scion, selected to marry Princess of Nansha—daughter of Emperor Jian of Liang.

sentences.zh: 陳受命，授中書侍郎，兼散騎常侍，與黃門郎王瑜使齊，數年不遣，天嘉初乃還。

translations.literal: When Chen received the mandate he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; with Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Wang Yu he was envoy to Qi and was not sent back for several years; only in the early Tianjia era did he return.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen received the mandate he became Director of the Palace Secretariat and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; with Wang Yu he was envoy to Qi and was not sent back for years; only in early Tianjia did he return.

sentences.zh: 太建三年，累遷御史中丞，羽林監。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taijian he was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian 3 he rose to Censor-in-Chief and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 時豫章王叔英不奉法度，逼取人馬，憲依事劾奏，免叔英。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Yuzhang Shuying did not observe law and regulation, forcibly taking men's horses; Xian impeached according to the facts and removed Shuying.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuying of Yuzhang did not observe law, forcibly taking horses; Xian impeached on the facts and removed him.

sentences.zh: 自是朝野嚴憚。

translations.literal: From this court and countryside were sternly in awe.
translations.idiomatic: From this court and countryside were sternly in awe.

sentences.zh: 憲詳練朝章，尤明聽斷，至有獄情未盡而有司具法者，即伺閑為帝言之，所申理甚眾。

translations.literal: Xian was thoroughly versed in court regulations and especially clear in hearing and deciding; when there were cases whose circumstances were not yet exhausted yet the offices had already prepared the law, he would seize leisure to speak to the emperor, and cases he clarified were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was thoroughly versed in court regulations and especially clear in judgment; when cases were not yet exhausted yet offices had prepared the law, he seized leisure to speak to the emperor, and cases he clarified were very many.

sentences.zh: 嘗陪宴承香合，賓退後，宣帝留憲與衛尉樊俊徙席山亭，談宴終日。

translations.literal: He once accompanied a feast at the Hall of Received Fragrance; after guests withdrew Emperor Xuan kept Xian and Commandant of the Guard Fan Jun, moved seats to a mountain pavilion, and feasted and talked all day.
translations.idiomatic: He once feasted at the Hall of Received Fragrance; after guests withdrew Emperor Xuan kept Xian and Commandant Fan Jun, moved to a mountain pavilion, and talked all day.

sentences.zh: 帝謂俊曰：「袁家故為有人。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Jun, "The Yuan house from old has had men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Jun, "The Yuan house from old has had men."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 自侍中遷吳郡太守，以父任固辭，改授南康內史。

translations.literal: From Palace Attendant he was transferred to Administrator of Wu Commandery; because of his father's post he firmly declined and was changed to Internal Administrator of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: From Palace Attendant he was offered Administrator of Wu Commandery; because of his father's post he declined and was changed Internal Administrator of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 憲以久居清顯，累表自求解任，帝曰：「諸人在職，屢有謗書，卿處事已多，可謂清白，別相甄錄，且勿致辭。」

translations.literal: Because he long dwelt in pure eminence he repeatedly memorialized requesting release from office; the emperor said, "Others in office repeatedly have memorials of slander; you have handled affairs very many and can be called pure and white—I separately shall examine and record; for now do not resign."
translations.idiomatic: Because he long dwelt in pure eminence he repeatedly requested release; the emperor said, "Others in office face slander; you have handled many affairs and can be called pure—I separately shall examine and record; for now do not resign."

sentences.zh: 遷右僕射，參掌選事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and shared in directing selection.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and shared in directing selection.

sentences.zh: 先是憲長兄樞為左僕射，至是憲為右僕射，台省目樞為大僕射，憲為小僕射，朝廷榮之。

translations.literal: Earlier Xian's elder brother Shu was Vice Director of the Left; now Xian was Vice Director of the Right—the palace offices called Shu the Great Vice Director and Xian the Small Vice Director; the court honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier elder brother Shu was Left Vice Director; now Xian was Right Vice Director—the palace called Shu Great Vice Director and Xian Small Vice Director; the court honored them.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝不豫，憲與吏部尚書毛喜俱受顧命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was ill, Xian together with Director of Personnel Mao Xi both received the final charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was ill, Xian and Director of Personnel Mao Xi both received the final charge.

sentences.zh: 始興王叔陵之肆逆也，憲指麾部分，預有力焉。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shixing Shuling committed outrage, Xian directed disposition and had a share in the strength of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shuling of Shixing committed outrage, Xian directed disposition and had a share in the strength of it.

sentences.zh: 後主被創病篤，執憲手曰：「我兒尚幼，後事委卿。

translations.literal: The Later Lord, wounded and gravely ill, grasped Xian's hand and said, "My son is still young; later affairs I entrust to you."
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord, wounded and gravely ill, grasped Xian's hand: "My son is still young; later affairs I entrust to you."

sentences.zh: 」憲曰：「群情喁喁，冀聖躬康復，後事之委，未敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Xian said, "The crowd's feeling is eager; I hope the sage person recovers; the entrustment of later affairs—I dare not receive the command."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The crowd's feeling is eager; I hope Your Majesty recovers; the entrustment of later affairs—I dare not receive the command."

sentences.zh: 以功封建安縣伯，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Jian'an and concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Earl of Jian'an and Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中、太子詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed as Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 及太子加元服，行釋奠禮，憲表請解職，不許，尋給扶二人。

translations.literal: When the crown prince added adult cap and performed the libation-and-sacrifice rite, Xian memorialized requesting release from office; it was not permitted; soon two supports were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince came of age and performed the libation rite, Xian requested release; it was refused; soon two supports were granted.

sentences.zh: 皇太子頗不率典訓，憲手錶陳諫十條，皆援引古今，言辭切直。

translations.literal: The crown prince quite did not follow canonical instruction; Xian by hand memorialized ten items of remonstrance, all citing past and present, with language cutting and straight.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince quite did not follow instruction; Xian memorialized ten items of remonstrance, all citing past and present, language cutting and straight.

sentences.zh: 太子雖外示容納，心無悛改。

translations.literal: The crown prince though outwardly showed acceptance inwardly had no mind to reform.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince outwardly showed acceptance but inwardly had no mind to reform.

sentences.zh: 後主欲立寵姬張貴妃子始安王為嗣，嘗從容言之，吏部尚書蔡征順旨稱讚，憲厲色折之曰：「皇太子國家儲副，億兆宅心，卿是何人，輕言廢立。

translations.literal: The Later Lord wished to establish favored consort Zhang Guifei's son Prince of Shi'an as heir; he once spoke of it at leisure; Director of Personnel Cai Zheng followed intent and praised; Xian with stern countenance rebuked him, saying, "The crown prince is the state's heir; the hundred millions dwell in heart—what man are you, lightly to speak of deposing and establishing?"
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord wished to establish favored consort Zhang Guifei's son Prince of Shi'an as heir and once spoke of it; Director Cai Zheng followed intent and praised; Xian sternly rebuked him: "The crown prince is the state's heir; the millions dwell in heart—what man are you, lightly to speak of deposing and establishing?"

sentences.zh: 」然是夏竟廢太子為吳興王。

translations.literal: Yet that summer the crown prince was at last deposed as Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that summer the crown prince was deposed as Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 後主知憲有規諫之事，歎曰：「袁德章實骨鯁臣。

translations.literal: The Later Lord knew Xian had matters of regulation and remonstrance and sighed, saying, "Yuan Dezhang is truly a bone-in-the-throat minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord knew Xian had remonstrated and sighed, "Yuan Dezhang is truly a bone-in-the-throat minister."

sentences.zh: 」即日詔為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: That same day an edict made him Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict made him Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，隋軍來伐，隋將賀若弼進燒宮城北掖門，兵衛皆散走，朝士各藏，唯憲侍左右。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Sui armies came to attack; Sui General Heluo Bi advanced burning the palace city's north Wing Gate; guards and defenders all scattered and fled; court gentlemen each hid—only Xian attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 3 Sui armies attacked; General Heluo Bi burned the palace city's north Wing Gate; guards scattered; court gentlemen hid—only Xian attended at his side.

sentences.zh: 後主謂曰：「我從來待卿不先餘人，今日見卿，可謂歲寒知松柏後凋也。

translations.literal: The Later Lord said to him, "I from the first treated you before all others; today seeing you, one may say that in cold years one knows the pine and cypress are last to wither."
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord said, "I from the first treated you before all others; today seeing you, one may say in cold years one knows pine and cypress are last to wither."

sentences.zh: 非唯由我無德，亦是江東衣冠道盡。

translations.literal: Not only because I am without virtue—it is also that east-of-the-river officialdom's Way is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Not only because I am without virtue—it is also that east-of-the-river officialdom's Way is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 」後主將避匿，憲正色曰：「北兵之入，必無所犯，大事如此，陛下安之？

translations.literal: The Later Lord was about to hide; Xian with stern countenance said, "When northern troops enter they will surely not violate; the great affair is thus—how can Your Majesty rest easy?"
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord was about to hide; Xian sternly said, "When northern troops enter they will not violate; the great affair is thus—how can Your Majesty rest easy?"

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下依梁武見侯景故事以待之。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to follow Emperor Wu of Liang's precedent in receiving Hou Jing and wait thus.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to follow Emperor Wu of Liang's precedent in receiving Hou Jing and wait thus.

sentences.zh: 」不從，因下榻馳去。

translations.literal: He did not follow; he therefore descended from the couch and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: He did not follow; he descended from the couch and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 憲從出後堂景陽殿，後主投井中，憲拜哭而出。

translations.literal: Xian followed out the rear hall Jingyang Pavilion; the Later Lord threw himself into a well; Xian bowed, wept, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Xian followed out the rear hall Jingyang Pavilion; the Later Lord threw himself into a well; Xian bowed, wept, and went out.

sentences.zh: 及至長安，隋文帝嘉其雅操，下詔以為江表稱首，授開府儀同三司、昌州刺史。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui praised his elegant integrity; an edict said he was chief among the south of the river and appointed him Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Cord and Prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an Emperor Wen of Sui praised his elegant integrity; an edict said he was chief among the south of the river and made him Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Cord and Prefect of Chang.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年，授晉王廣府長史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Chief Clerk to Prince of Jin Guang's household.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 14 he was chief clerk to Prince Guang of Jin's household.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，時年七十，贈大將軍、安成郡公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died, then aged seventy; posthumously made Grand General and Duke of Ancheng Commandery; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he died, aged seventy; posthumously made Grand General and Duke of Ancheng; posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 長子承家，仕隋至秘書丞、國子司業。

translations.literal: Eldest son Chengjia served Sui reaching Secretary of the Secretariat and Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Chengjia served Sui to Secretary of the Secretariat and Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 君正弟 敬

translations.literal: Junzheng's younger brother Jing
translations.idiomatic: Junzheng's younger brother Jing

sentences.zh: 敬字子恭，純素有風格。

translations.literal: Jing, styled Zigong, was pure and plain with style and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, courtesy name Zigong, was pure and plain with style and bearing.

sentences.zh: 幼便篤學，老而無倦。

translations.literal: From youth he was devoted to learning; in old age without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth devoted to learning; in old age without weariness.

sentences.zh: 仕梁位太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he reached Supervisor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he reached Supervisor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，流寓嶺表。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling he drifted in exile beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Jiangling he drifted in exile beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，敬在廣州依歐陽頠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, Jing was in Guangzhou relying on Ouyang Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's Emperor Wu received the abdication, Jing was in Guangzhou relying on Ouyang Pi.

sentences.zh: 頠卒，其子紇據州，將有異志，敬累諫不從。

translations.literal: When Pi died his son He seized the province and was about to harbor a different intent; Jing repeatedly remonstrated and was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi died his son He seized the province and harbored different intent; Jing repeatedly remonstrated and was not followed.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，遣章昭達討紇，紇將敗，恨不納敬言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne he sent Zhang Zhaoda to attack He; when He was about to be defeated he regretted not accepting Jing's words.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he sent Zhang Zhaoda against He; when He was about to fall he regretted not accepting Jing's words.

sentences.zh: 朝廷義之，徵為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: The court honored his righteousness and summoned him as Supervisor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his righteousness and summoned him Supervisor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歷左戶、都官二尚書，太常卿，散騎常侍，金紫光祿大夫，加特進。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Left Household and Director of Punishments, Minister of Ceremonies, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and was additionally made Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Left Household and Director of Punishments, Minister of Ceremonies, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord, and was additionally Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 至德三年，卒，諡靖德子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhide he died; posthumous title Viscount Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 3 he died; posthumous title Viscount Jingde.

sentences.zh: 子元友嗣。

translations.literal: Son Yuanyou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuanyou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 敬弟泌。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Bi.

sentences.zh: 泌字文洋，清正有幹局，容體魁岸，志行修謹。

translations.literal: Bi, styled Wenyang, was upright and pure with capacity for affairs; his stature was tall and imposing; his will and conduct were cultivated and careful.
