translations.idiomatic: Bi, courtesy name Wenyang, was upright and pure with capacity for affairs; tall and imposing; will and conduct cultivated and careful.

sentences.zh: 仕梁曆諸王府佐。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he held staff posts in various princely households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he held staff posts in various princely households.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，泌兄君正為吳郡太守，梁簡文帝在東宮，板泌為東宮領直，令往吳中，召募士卒。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Bi's elder brother Junzheng was Administrator of Wu Commandery; Emperor Jian of Liang in the Eastern Palace commissioned Bi as Eastern Palace Direct Attendant and ordered him to go to Wu to recruit soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion elder brother Junzheng was Administrator of Wu; Emperor Jian in the Eastern Palace commissioned Bi Direct Attendant and ordered him to Wu to recruit soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及景圍台城，泌率所領赴援。

translations.literal: When Jing besieged the capital platform city, Bi led those under his command to go to aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing besieged the capital, Bi led his command to aid.

sentences.zh: 城陷，依鄱陽嗣王範。

translations.literal: When the city fell he relied on Prince of Poyang Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he relied on Prince Fan of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 范卒，泌降景。

translations.literal: When Fan died Bi surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan died Bi surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，王僧辯表泌為富春太守，兼丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified Wang Sengbian memorialized Bi as Administrator of Fuchun and concurrently Prefect of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified Wang Sengbian memorialized Bi Administrator of Fuchun and concurrently Prefect of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 貞陽侯明僭位，以為侍中，使于齊。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Zhenyang Ming usurped the throne he was made Palace Attendant and sent as envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis Ming of Zhenyang usurped the throne Bi was made Palace Attendant and envoy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，泌自齊從梁永嘉王莊往王琳所。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, Bi from Qi followed Liang's Prince of Yongjia Zhuang to Wang Lin's place.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's Emperor Wu received the abdication, Bi from Qi followed Liang's Prince Zhuang of Yongjia to Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 及莊稱尊號，以泌為侍中、丞相長史。

translations.literal: When Zhuang declared the imperial title, Bi was made Palace Attendant and Chief Clerk to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang declared the imperial title, Bi was made Palace Attendant and chief clerk to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，眾皆散，唯泌輕舟送達於北境，屬莊于御史中丞劉仲威，然後拜辭歸陳請罪，文帝深義之。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated the crowd all scattered; only Bi in a light boat escorted Zhuang to the northern border, entrusted Zhuang to Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei, and then bowed in leave and returned to Chen to request punishment; Emperor Wen deeply honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was defeated the crowd scattered; only Bi in a light boat escorted Zhuang to the northern border, entrusted Zhuang to Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei, bowed in leave, returned to Chen to request punishment; Emperor Wen deeply honored his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 累遷通直散騎常侍，兼侍中，聘周。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Palace Attendant, envoy to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant, envoy to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝入輔，以泌為司徒左長史，卒於官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Bi was made Chief Clerk of the Left to the Minister of Education and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, Bi was chief clerk of the left to the Minister of Education and died in office.

sentences.zh: 臨終戒其子芳華曰：「吾於朝廷素無功績，瞑目之後，斂手足旋葬，無得受贈諡。

translations.literal: Near death he charged his son Fanghua, saying, "I toward the court from old have no achievement; after closing eyes, gather hands and feet and bury at once—do not receive posthumous enfeoffment or title."
translations.idiomatic: Near death he charged son Fanghua: "I toward the court from old have no achievement; after closing eyes, gather hands and feet and bury at once—do not receive posthumous enfeoffment or title."

sentences.zh: 」其子述泌遺意，朝廷不許，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰質。

translations.literal: His son stated Bi's final intent; the court would not permit it and posthumously made him Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord; posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son stated Bi's final intent; the court would not permit refusal and posthumously made him Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Cord; posthumous title Zhi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：天長地久，四時代謝，靈化悠遠，生不再來，所以據洪圖而輕天下，吝寸陰而賤尺璧。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Heaven long, earth enduring—the four seasons replace one another; spirit transformation is far and deep; life does not come again; therefore men holding great designs lightly treat the realm, stingy with an inch of shadow and cheapening a foot of jade.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Heaven long, earth enduring—the four seasons turn; spirit runs far and deep; life does not come again; therefore men holding great designs lightly treat the realm, stingy with time and cheapening jade.

sentences.zh: 夫義重於生，空傳前誥，投軀徇主，罕遇其人。

translations.literal: Righteousness weighs heavier than life—empty transmission in earlier edicts; casting the body to follow the lord—rarely does one meet such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness weighs heavier than life—empty in earlier edicts; casting the body to follow the lord—rarely does one meet such a man.

sentences.zh: 觀夫宋、齊以還，袁門世蹈忠義，固知風霜之概、松筠其性乎。

translations.literal: Looking from Song and Qi onward, the Yuan gate generation after generation treads loyalty and righteousness—one truly knows the wind of frost and that pine and bamboo are their nature.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi onward, the Yuan house generation after generation treads loyalty and righteousness—one truly knows frost's wind and that pine and bamboo are their nature.

sentences.zh: 若無陽源之節，丹青夫何取貴。

translations.literal: Had there not been Yangyuan's integrity, how would cinnabar take its worth?
translations.idiomatic: Had there not been Yangyuan's integrity, how would cinnabar take its worth?

sentences.zh: 顗雖末路披猖，原心有本。

translations.literal: Yan though at the end of the road ran wild, in original heart had root.
translations.idiomatic: Yan though at the end ran wild, in original heart had root.

sentences.zh: 彖之出處所蹈，實懋家風。

translations.literal: In Bian's going out and staying and what he treads, he truly honors the family wind.
translations.idiomatic: In Bian's going out and staying and what he treads, he truly honors the family wind.

sentences.zh: 粲執履之跡，近乎仁勇，古人所謂疾風勁草，豈此之謂乎？

translations.literal: Can's holding and treading of conduct nearly reaches benevolence and courage—what the ancients call fierce wind and stiff grass—is this not the saying?
translations.idiomatic: Can's conduct nearly reaches benevolence and courage—what ancients call fierce wind and stiff grass—is this not the saying?

sentences.zh: 昔王經峻節，既被旌于晉世，粲之貞固，亦改葬于齊朝，其激厲之方，異代同符者矣。

translations.literal: In old times Wang Jing's stern integrity was already honored in Jin times; Can's steadfast firmness was also given changed burial in Qi times—their methods of stirring and sharpening, different ages with the same tally.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing's stern integrity was honored in Jin; Can's steadfast firmness received changed burial in Qi—their methods of stirring courage, different ages with the same tally.

sentences.zh: 昂命屬崩離，身逢危季，雖獨夫喪德，臣節無改。

translations.literal: Ang's fate belonged to collapse and separation; his person met a dangerous season; though the lone tyrant lost virtue, minister's integrity did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's fate belonged to collapse; his person met a dangerous season; though the lone tyrant lost virtue, minister's integrity did not change.

sentences.zh: 拒梁武之命，義烈存焉，隆從兄之服，悌心高已。

translations.literal: He refused Emperor Wu of Liang's command—righteous fierceness remained; he wore mourning for a cousin from afar—fraternal heart rose higher still.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Liang's Emperor Wu—righteous fierceness remained; he wore mourning for a distant cousin—fraternal heart rose higher still.

sentences.zh: 既而抗言儲嗣，無忘直道，辭榮身後，有心黜殯。

translations.literal: Then he spoke against the heir—without forgetting the straight Way; he declined glory after death—had mind to abolish lavish burial.
translations.idiomatic: Then he spoke against the heir—without forgetting the straight Way; he declined glory after death—had mind to abolish lavish burial.

sentences.zh: 自初及末，無虧風範，從微至著，皆為稱職，蓋一代之名公也。

translations.literal: From first to last without failing in style and measure, from slight to manifest all were fitting to office—truly a great lord of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: From first to last without failing in style, from slight to manifest all fitting to office—truly a great lord of a generation.

sentences.zh: 樞風格峻整，憲仁義率由，韓子稱「人臣委質，心無有二」，憲弗渝歲暮，良可稱云。

translations.literal: Shu's style was stern and ordered, Xian's benevolence and righteousness followed constant rule; Han Fei says "the minister entrusts his person and in heart has no second"—Xian did not change at year's end; truly he may be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's style was stern and ordered, Xian's benevolence and righteousness followed constant rule; Han Fei says "the minister entrusts his person and in heart has no second"—Xian did not change at year's end; truly he may be praised.

sentences.zh: 敬、泌立履之地，亦不為替矣。

translations.literal: In the ground where Jing and Bi stood and tread, they also were not inferior.
translations.idiomatic: In the ground where Jing and Bi stood and tread, they also were not inferior.
